body:
Follow-up of #2597.

The fix for #2597 cuts a new, larger outline from Top Z down, one stepdown at a time. The contour generator gets no stock region. So it takes the material outside the part to stand up to Top Z.

Where the stock is narrow, the added passes cut air. This is safe, but it costs time.

Proposal:
- Give the stock region (the stock outline at each level) to the whole-model contour.
- Start each new ring at the first level where its tool sweep meets stock that is not cut.
- Keep the refusal by name when a ring cannot be proven clear.

Files: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_whole_reach.rs` (`reach_up`), and the app code that builds `ContourParams`.

This work is under the safety floor: it can change posted G-code.

title: Verify reports a false gouge when a Face row ends near the open outer rim after a lift over a hole

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

A Face lifts over a hole of its region. The row piece beside the hole ends a tool radius off the hole. If the hole is near the open outer rim of the region, that end is less than a tool radius from the rim. Verify law (b) reports the move as `cuts past the finish surface`. The finding blocks the post.

The finding is false. No part material stands above the cut plane at that rim. The outer rim of a Face is open: its rows cross the rim by design.

## Expected

No finding for a Face move whose end is near an open rim. A move near a wall (part material above the cut plane) is still reported.

## Repro

- Part: a plate 40 x 60 x 10 mm centred on the origin (z 0..10). One dia 6 through-hole at (-12, 0).
- Stock: a box 40 x 60 x 12 mm (z 0..12).
- Tool: `EM-1000-4FL` (dia 10).
- Operation: Face, source the part, `holes: lift` (the default), Cut Z fixed 10, stepover 4, clearance 30.

Result on upstream main 1ae4d061f with the fix of #2437 applied: 5 plunges, and `Gouge` findings at moves 15, 18, 27 and 30. Move 15 is the plunge at X -18.227 Y -5 after the lift. It is 1.77 mm inside the rim at X -20.

## Cause (found during #2437)

`sim::verify::section::tangency` reads each law point against all loops of `cx.region` with the distance floor `r - tol`. In `Mode::Boundary` with a model, it does not ask if the region edge is a wall. `wall_gouge` in the same file has that classification for the whole-move reading (a region edge is a wall when the model section holds a probe beside the edge midpoint).

## Workaround

Use `holes: through` or `holes: cut_air` when the holes are air, or use a stock source.

## Notes

- This is a change to a gouge law. It needs a pin that a wall below the model top is still reported.
- #2437 removed the lifts for holes below the cut plane. This defect stays for holes at the cut plane.

**Done means:** a Face that lifts over a hole near the open outer rim has no finding; a test pins it, and a second test pins that a move within a tool radius of a wall is still reported.

body:
## What happens

A Thread operation on a through hole that `detect_holes` finds does not post. The verification report convicts each helix move with "move N cuts past the finish surface".

## How to see it

1. Make a plate 40 x 40 x 10 mm with one through hole, radius 3.3235 mm (96 facets around).
2. Add the catalog tool `TM-0600-P125`.
3. Add a Thread operation with the plate as source. Use the hole that `detect_holes` gives (through: true).
4. Generate and verify.

Result: the verify gate is not empty. Each helix move has the gouge message.

## What we know

- A blind hole of the same radius (`entry_z` at the top, `floor_z` 4.0, `through: false`) verifies and posts without a problem. The test `hole_feed_rating` (PR for #2598) uses that layout for this reason.
- The cause is not investigated. Possible causes are the helix below the part floor on a through hole, or the finish surface of the faceted hole wall.
- It is not known if the conviction is correct. If the path really cuts into the wall, the defect is in the generator. If it does not, the defect is in the judgement.

## Expected

A thread mill on a through hole that fits the tool posts, or the refusal names the real cause.

Found during #2598.

Found during #2201 (PR #2652).

After the path line cache, `frame/collect` still takes about 2.7-4 ms for each frame with an 8114-move path shown or selected. The named spans in `collect` add up to about 1 ms only.

Likely causes (not measured one by one):
- `path_overlay::toolpath_lines` copies the cached lines into a new vector.
- `interact::collect_overlay` and `world::collect_overlay` copy that vector again, and each calls `capped`.
- `world::world_verts_by` clones the cached model vertices on each frame.

Expected: add spans to find the cost, then keep the overlay as shared slices (for example `Arc` parts) so that a still frame copies nothing. Keep the counter tests of crates/ui/AGENTS.md "Frame cost".

title: Sodick wire post: no runnable pass structure for LN1/LN2/LN3 controls (C000 entry, C001 rough, C002 sizing)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Reported by a Sodick wire EDM owner (@spikeypineapple) on #617, 2026-11-16:

> I can say for sure this won't work. It might work on older machines, but it won't run on a ln1/ln2/ln3 control (anything made in the last 20 years).

**What the LN controls expect** (his report): the condition codes follow the passes:
- `C000` - entering the cut (a stable condition, so the wire does not break)
- `C001` - rough cut
- `C002` - sizing / second cut
- `C903` and up - polishing passes

**What the post does now** (`assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps`, main 1ae4d061f):
- writes ONE condition word per operation, the operation's own condition id (`C` + three digits), line 296;
- refuses a condition change between passes (skims), line 186, and sends skims to `wire-iso` instead;
- writes no entry condition before the cut.

So a normal 1- or 2-pass part on a current Sodick cannot be posted as the control expects. Nothing gouges, and the workaround (`wire-iso`, or one operation per pass) exists, so P3 by the AGENTS.md table.

**Scope** (his suggestion): 2 passes first - entry `C000`, rough `C001`, sizing `C002`. Polishing (`C903+`) later.

**Open questions for the reporter** (asked on #617): where in the program each C word goes (on the threading/entry move, at each pass start); whether `C000` is used for every start hole; an example program from an LN control (his earlier AQ600L example on #617 shows a condition table in the header).

Clean-room: no CAM vendor's Sodick post or output is used; only the owner's own description and public Sodick manuals.

Done means: the Sodick post writes the C000/C001/C002 structure for a 1- and 2-pass Wire Contour, pinned by golden programs, and the owner confirms on an LN control (or the open questions are answered on this issue).

Part of #617. Related: #1500 (LN program format), #2130.

title: Viewport: add "Shaded, no edges" and a see-through wireframe display mode

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
The maintainer asked for this work, in his own words (2026-11-18):

> issue; p4; there is shaded and wireframe today. There should be a shaded with no edges, and wireframe "see thru" as well.

## State of the code

The Browser pane has a "Solids" choice with two modes (`DisplayMode` in `crates/ui/src/state.rs`, radios in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/browser_pane.rs`):

- `ShadedEdges`: flat-shaded faces with the CAD wire over them. It is the default.
- `Wireframe`: faces go to the depth buffer only, so the model reads as a hidden-line drawing. Hidden edges do not show.

## Wanted

Four display modes:

1. **Shaded** (with edges). The current default. No change.
2. **Shaded, no edges.** Faces only. No CAD wire over them. Edges of a picked or hovered feature still show, so that picking stays visible.
3. **Wireframe** (hidden lines removed). The current mode. No change.
4. **Wireframe, see-through.** Every edge draws, front and back, with no hidden-line removal. The model does not hide the stock, the fixtures or the toolpath behind it. Hidden edges may draw in a lighter tone, so the front stays readable.

Details:
- The choice stays one control in the Browser pane. Four radios or one drop-down. Plain English labels: "Shaded", "Shaded, no edges", "Wireframe", "Wireframe, see-through". Tooltips say what each does.
- The mode is view state (a direct field flip, never a command), as today. It applies to the model, the stock and the fixtures in the same way. The toolpath and the simulation stock follow their own rules and stay readable in each mode.
- The setting is saved with the other view settings, if the others are saved. An old file without the field loads with the default.
- Picking works in each mode. In "Wireframe, see-through" a click picks the edge nearest to the cursor, front or back, with the nearest to the camera first. State the rule in the test.
- The renderer builds the edge and face passes once for each geometry change (precalculate and cache; frame target under 10 ms). No per-frame rebuild of the edge lists.

## Constraints

- A UI PR needs before and after screenshots of all four modes in the PR body. Tests assert labels, roles, which mode is selected, the state field and the picking rule. They do not assert pixels. Pixel snapshots are release-lane only and a PR never changes a PNG.
- Update the layout test of the Browser page. Keep each file under about 400 lines.
- `DisplayMode` is also used by the wasm build. The new modes must work there.

## Done means

- A test shows that each radio sets its mode and that the labels exist.
- A test shows the draw list for each mode: faces and edges as listed above.
- A test shows picking in "Wireframe, see-through" with the stated rule.
- The PR has the screenshots.

title: test(app): the v63 drill test in sketch_project.rs does not load a real v63 file

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Found in the delta review of PR #2134 (comment 6993126790). The test arrives with that PR.

## Problem

`crates/app/tests/sketch_project.rs:176-204`, `a_v63_break_through_file_steps_up_without_losing_the_stated_limit`, makes its "v63" fixture from a save of the current build. Then it sets `version` to 63.

Since main's v68 (#2441), each saved Drill row has the `break_through_from` key. A real v63 file cannot have this key. Thus:
- `settle_drill_break_through` (`crates/app/src/project/params_impl.rs:2475`) does not change the row.
- The test does not check the v63 -> v68 drill step (the absent key reads as `Tip`).
- The test checks only that a stated `break_through: 0.0` survives.

`crates/app/tests/break_through.rs` (`v65_preserves_cutting_steps_and_loads_v63_break_through_and_v62_defaults`) covers the real step. It removes `break_through_from` below v68 and expects `Tip`.

## Fix

Do one of these:
1. Remove `break_through_from` from the Drill row of the fixture before the load. Expect `BreakThroughFrom::Tip` on the loaded operation. Expect `break_through_from: "tip"` (or the saved spelling) in the saved file.
2. Rename the test to say what it checks: a stated zero break-through survives a step-up.

Do this after PR #2134 merges.

title: Viewport: draw an arrow and the text "Operator side" at the work envelope

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
The maintainer asked for this work, in his own words (2026-11-18):

> issue, p4, in the work envelope. there should be a Arrow "pointing" towards the user and the text stating "operator side".. so people understand where they look "into" the work envelope from.

## Problem

The viewport shows the work envelope of the machine. A user cannot tell from which side the operator looks into it. The user then does not know how the part sits, how the vise faces, or which way is "front".

## Wanted

1. The work envelope shows an arrow on the operator side. The arrow points toward the operator, away from the envelope. The text "Operator side" is next to the arrow.
2. The side comes from the machine. A 3-axis mill and a 4-axis or 5-axis machine have a default operator side (the front of the machine). A lathe, a router table, a laser or a plasma table can differ. The machine file may name the side. When it does not, a documented default for the machine type applies. A decision file in `docs/decisions/` records the defaults.
3. The arrow and the text follow the view: the text stays readable, the arrow stays at the envelope edge in 3D, and both do not hide the part or the toolpath. Draw them with the envelope, in the envelope colour or a muted one.
4. A switch hides them. Default: shown. The switch is a view setting (ephemeral UI state, no undo command). It sits with the other envelope display options.
5. The label text is plain English and is the same in all views. No G-code words.

## Constraints

- Layers: ui reads the machine data through the app API. A new machine-file field follows the machine-file rules and keeps old files valid (the field is optional).
- No per-frame work that can be cached (frame target under 10 ms). Build the arrow geometry once for each envelope change.
- A UI PR needs before and after screenshots in the PR body. Tests assert the presence, the text, the side for each machine type and the switch state, not pixel values. Update the layout test of the viewport page if it applies.
- Draw an original arrow. Use no asset from another product.

## Done means

- A test shows the arrow and the text for a mill, with the side as the default says.
- A test shows a machine file that names another side, and that an old file without the field still loads.
- A test shows that the switch hides and shows them.
- The PR has before and after screenshots.

body:
Part of #2607 (slice S5 of 6).

The order of the maintainer (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority".

## What
Replace the dense GPU lattice with a sparse brick pool and a page table (Hoetzlein, GVDB, HPG 2016; Crassin et al., GigaVoxels, I3D 2009).

- The dense lattice limits the display cell. Example: a 200 x 150 x 60 mm block at 0.25 mm is 460 MB for one f32 layer. This does not fit the 128 MiB default `maxStorageBufferBindingSize`.
- The CPU makes the brick work list (S1, #2626). The GPU allocates and fills the bricks.
- The trace shader reads through the page table.
- The display cell follows the pixel size. `DEFAULT_TEXELS` in `crates/app/src/stock_view.rs` (line 39) is then for the CPU path only.

## Tests
- Parity: the sparse pool against the dense lattice on the same program, bit equal in the touched cells.
- Measure on the large fixtures in release, against the frame target (#2238, under 10 ms for each frame). Write the readings in the PR.
- Out of memory: refuse by name, and the dense or CPU path runs.

Blocked by #2629 (S3).

Done means: the GPU playback uses a sparse pool, shows a finer cell than today within the memory limits, and the parity tests and measurements are in the PR.

## What
Use the S2 kernel (#2627) for the viewport playback.

- The kernel writes the `Scene.cut` storage buffer of `crates/ui/src/trace.rs` directly. On the GPU path, the CPU pack and the patch upload (`trace.rs` lines 229 and 236-243) do not run.
- Keyframes are GPU buffer copies, within a VRAM budget. A seek copies the nearest keyframe and dispatches the remaining moves.
- Generation runs outside the frame (#2238: frame target under 10 ms).
- On `DeviceLost` or any error, the CPU playback runs. Log it one time. `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off` (#2620) turns the GPU path off.

- End-frame parity on the software adapter: the GPU playback picture against the CPU playback picture, within the eye tolerance of `crates/ui/tests/trace_parity.rs`.
- A fault test: a forced kernel error gives the CPU picture.
- The `camcraft-ui` lib tests stay green. The `#[test]` count does not go down.

Display only. The verdict (`crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` `simulate_document`) and the post gate do not change.

Blocked by #2627 (S2) and #2611. #2611 is a user bug: the voxel playback shows no visible removal. A parity test against a broken CPU picture has no value.

UI PR: add before and after screenshots to the PR body.

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat (2026-11-18), in his own words:

> bug, when on wcs page, using the set wcs from feature.. u cannot pich each feature correctly.. From a useability feature.. there should be four pick buttons, one for each, z,x,y,origin..  so we dont have to use a dropdown.. it should be clearly a small "table" for it, and then a apply/clear button under the four selections.

## What happens

On the WCS page, the "Set WCS from features" block picks one role at a time through a dropdown. The user cannot pick each feature correctly. The report does not say which pick fails. The worker finds out (see the first steps).

## Wanted

1. A small table with four rows, one for each role: Origin, X axis, Y axis, Z axis.
2. Each row has its own pick button. No dropdown chooses the role. The row shows what is picked (a plain-English name of the feature, not an internal id; see #2403) or "not set".
3. A pick button starts a pick for its own role. A click in the viewport fills that row only. A second pick for the same row replaces it. A row can be cleared alone.
4. Under the table: one "Apply" button and one "Clear" button. "Apply" is enabled only when the picks are enough to define a WCS (for example, an origin, or the axis picks that the existing rules accept). Say in a tooltip what is missing when it is disabled. "Clear" empties all four rows.
5. Apply is one undoable command (the WCS from the setup stays the single source: `setup::wcs_slot`, no second derivation). A conflict between picks (for example X parallel to Z) is refused with a plain message at Apply, not accepted.
6. The page keeps its layout test and its pick tests. UI text is plain English.

## First steps for the worker

1. Reproduce the pick failure. Read `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_pick_row.rs`, `setup_settings_page.rs` and the tests `wcs_page_picks.rs` and `wcs_pick_tests.rs`. Find which pick goes to the wrong role or is dropped (for example a face, an edge, a vertex or a circle centre; see #701, #739, #1562).
2. Fix that defect with a pinning test, in the same PR as the new table or in a first commit.
3. Build the four-row table. Keep each file under about 400 lines.

## Constraints

- AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command": a pick is ephemeral UI state until Apply. Apply and Clear that changes the setup go through the undoable command. The MCP tool for set WCS from feature picks exists (#937). It stays and uses the same command.
- A UI PR needs before and after screenshots in the PR body. Tests assert labels, roles, enabled state and commands, not pixel values. Update `layout_page_wcs` if it exists.
- Do not use the `fig8.camproj` or `testpart.sc` user files in any test or screenshot.

## Done means

- A test shows that each of the four pick buttons fills its own row, for each feature kind that the page accepts.
- A test shows that Apply writes the expected WCS, that undo restores it, and that a conflicting set is refused.
- A test shows that Clear empties the four rows.
- The PR has the before and after screenshots.

body:
Part of #2526 (GPU shader toolpath generation). Slice 4 of 5. Needs #2620 (compute seam).

Maintainer order (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority". Thus this issue is `P4`.

## Why
The facet gouge law measures the exact distance between each ball-center segment and each model triangle (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/gouge.rs`: `facet_gouge` lines 43-172, `dist_seg_tri` line 174). Facets are already put in XY bins (lines 65-131). On a very long program against a very large mesh the pair count is still high.

## What
- A compute kernel marks the (segment, bin) pairs whose conservative distance is below `r + margin`. f32, tile-relative coordinates, margin larger than the stated f32 error bound.
- The CPU measures every marked pair with the f64 `dist_seg_tri`. The gouge depth and its location stay the f64 values.
- The kernel only removes pairs. It never adds a gouge, and it never sets a depth.
- With no GPU, or with the GPU off, `facet_gouge` runs as today.

## Prime Directive
- A gouge must block the post. An unmarked pair that has a gouge is the one risk. Thus the filter is a superset test, and it has a CPU parity test.
- Fault injection test: a kernel margin set to a negative value must make the parity test fail. The test proves that the parity test can catch a miss.

## Pinning tests (CPU reference)
- For the gouge fixtures of the sim suites, the GPU-marked pair set is a superset of the CPU pairs with distance below `r`.
- The gouge verdicts (depth, location, refusal text) are the same with the GPU on and off.
- Skip and fail policy of `headless_gpu` (#615, `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1`).

## Decision entry
Yes, if `camcraft-sim` gets an edge onto the compute crate of #2620. Recommended instead: the app computes the pair mask and passes it to `facet_gouge` as a value, so `camcraft-sim` stays GPU-free.

Effort: `effort:max` (gouge check; safety floor).

Done means: the GPU pair filter feeds `facet_gouge`, the verdicts are equal with the GPU on and off, the superset and fault injection tests pass, and the PR states the time readings on a long program.

body:
Part of #2526 (GPU shader toolpath generation). Slice 3 of 5. Needs #2619 (CPU facet grid) and #2620 (compute seam).

Maintainer order (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority". Thus this issue is `P4`.

## What
- A compute kernel computes, for each cell of a tile, a conservative bound of the ball support height: the inverse tool offset of the facets on a grid (M. Inui, "Fast inverse offset computation using polygon rendering hardware", Computer-Aided Design 35(2), 2003; the Z-map model of B. K. Choi and R. B. Jerard, "Sculptured Surface Machining", 1998).
- f32, tile-relative coordinates. The margin is larger than the stated f32 error bound of the kernel (WGSL "Floating Point Accuracy": division 2.5 ULP, `inverseSqrt` 2 ULP). The PR states the bound and how the margin covers it.
- The CPU uses the bound only to skip facets in `support_at` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/support.rs` 368-388) that cannot be the highest support.
- The posted height stays the f64 `support_at` value at the true sample point. `ball_clear` (lines 132-142) stays the certifier, in f64, against every facet of the CPU grid near the ball. The GPU never removes a facet from `ball_clear`.
- The app makes the GPU result in the generate job (`crates/app/src/commands/operation/generate.rs`), once for each operation, and passes it to motion as a value. Never in a frame. The CLI and MCP use the same path.
- With no GPU, or with the GPU off, motion runs the #2619 CPU path. The result is the same bytes.

## Prime Directive
- A wrong bound can only skip the true support. Then `ball_clear` refuses the lower candidate, and the march searches higher or refuses by name. A GPU error cannot make a gouge pass. A test pins this with a deliberately wrong bound (a fault injection test).
- The tolerance is not tied to the grid resolution. The grid only filters.

## Pinning tests (CPU reference)
- GPU on and GPU off give the same `.cl` and `.cnc` bytes on the 3D finishing goldens of `crates/app/tests/golden/`. Run on the software adapter; on hardware where present.
- The fault injection test above: a bound raised by a large value gives a refusal or the same output, never a lower cutter.
- Skip and fail policy of `headless_gpu` (#615, `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1`).

## Readings
Time of one large 3D finishing operation: CPU grid only (#2619) against CPU grid plus GPU filter, release build, with upload and readback times. If the GPU does not gain on the large fixtures, the PR says so and the switch stays off by default.

## Decision entry
Only if a new crate edge is added past the ones of #2620.

Effort: `effort:max` (toolpath geometry algorithm on a new compute path; safety floor).

Done means: the GPU bound filters the support scan, the goldens are byte-equal with the GPU on and off, the fault injection test passes, and the PR states the readings.

body:
Part of #2526 (GPU shader toolpath generation). Slice 2 of 5. Needs slice 1 (#2619) for the CPU reference.

Maintainer order (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority". Thus this issue is `P4`.

## Why
Only `camcraft-ui` links wgpu today, through the `egui_wgpu::wgpu` re-export (`Cargo.toml` lines 46-47). The generators run in `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-motion`, and in the CLI and MCP with no window. They have no GPU access. The headless device policy exists, but in `crates/ui/src/headless_gpu.rs`.

## What
- A new crate (recommended name `camcraft-gpu`) for headless compute. It holds:
  - The device policy of `headless_gpu.rs` (software adapter first in tests, then hardware), moved down from `camcraft-ui`. `camcraft-ui` then uses it.
  - A capability probe: `DownlevelFlags::COMPUTE_SHADERS`, `max_storage_buffer_binding_size`, `max_compute_workgroup_storage_size`. WebGL2 and GL below ES 3.1 have no compute: the probe says "no compute" by name.
  - One device for each process, made on the first request and cached (`OnceLock`). Never made for each operation or each frame.
  - A switch to turn the GPU off (recommended: `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off`) for tests and for machines with bad drivers (#2424, #74).
  - One kernel: conservative facet binning. Input: facet boxes in tile-relative f32, padded by `r` plus a margin. Output: the cell lists.
- The CPU path runs, with the same result, when there is no adapter, the probe fails, the device is lost, or a buffer is past the limit. The log names the reason one time. Never a panic, never `unwrap` on a GPU future.

## Pinning tests (CPU reference)
- Superset parity: for the same facets, each facet in the CPU grid cell of #2619 is in the GPU cell list. Extra GPU entries are permitted.
- Refusals: a buffer past the limit, and a forced "no compute" probe, give `Err` with the reason. The caller uses the CPU grid.
- Adapter policy: the `headless_gpu` rule (#615). No adapter prints a loud SKIP. `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` turns the skip into a failure. The self-hosted runners have the Mesa software drivers (`runners` skill), so the lane runs on lavapipe there.

## Decision entry and dependencies
- A `docs/decisions/` entry is necessary: new crate edges (`camcraft-ui` and `camcraft-app` onto the new crate). The entry lists the imported items and what rebuilds.
- A direct `wgpu` dependency is new for the workspace. The version must be the one that the egui set pins (`=30.0.1` with egui-wgpu `=0.36.2`), so no second wgpu enters the lock. The review sets `needs-maintainer` for this dependency, by AGENTS.md.
- The wgpu version then moves with the egui set (#658, #1118). The decision entry says so.
- `camcraft-motion` gets no GPU dependency. The app computes the GPU result and passes it into motion as a value.

Effort: `effort:high` (several crates, new behaviour with its tests). No posted output changes in this slice.

Done means: the new crate exists with the probe, the cached device, the CPU fallback and the binning kernel; the superset parity test passes on the software adapter; `camcraft-ui` uses the moved device policy; the decision entry is in the PR.

body:
Part of #2526 (GPU shader toolpath generation). Slice 1 of 5.

Maintainer order (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority". Thus this issue is `P4`.

## Why
The ball drop-cutter of 3D finishing tests every facet for each sample. `support_at` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/support.rs` lines 368-388) loops over all `Sup` entries with a padded box reject only. Each accepted candidate calls `ball_clear` (lines 132-142), which loops over all facets again. `column_clear` (line 162) does the same. There is no spatial index. The cost is about samples x facets.

The GPU filter of #2526 must match a CPU reference. This slice makes that reference: a CPU grid of facets that the GPU result is tested against. It is also the largest speed gain (estimate in #2526, comment 3/4).

## What
- Bin the `Sup` entries (from `build_sups`, lines 27-50) into a uniform XY grid by their padded box (`xmin..xmax`, `ymin..ymax`, already padded by `r`).
- `support_at`, `ball_clear`, `column_clear` and the fold scan (`edge.rs` `fold_best`) read only the facets of the cells that the query touches.
- The same f64 functions run. The subset must hold every facet whose padded box contains the query point. This keeps the result the same bits.
- Optional, same PR or a follow-up: run the raster lines in parallel with an order-preserving `collect`.
- No GPU code in this slice.

## Prime Directive
- The grid is conservative: a facet goes into each cell that its padded box touches. A bin miss would let `ball_clear` pass a ball that touches a facet. A test pins the superset rule.
- Degenerate input (NaN box, zero-area facet, a box past the coordinate guard) goes to every cell or gives a clean `GenError`. It never panics.

## Pinning tests (CPU reference)
- The 3D finishing goldens in `crates/app/tests/golden/` give the same `.cl` and `.cnc` bytes as before.
- A new motion test: for random sample points over a fixture, the grid query answers the same `support_at` and `ball_clear` values as the full scan.
- A new motion test: each facet whose padded box contains a point is in the grid query of that point (superset law).

## Readings
Measure the time of one large 3D finishing operation before and after (release build). Put the numbers in the PR body.

## Decision entry
Not needed if the change stays inside `camcraft-motion`. No new crate edge, no new dependency.

Effort: `effort:high` by the safety floor (toolpath generation and its gouge certifier).

Done means: the 3D finishing support scan uses a facet grid, the goldens are byte-equal, the superset and parity tests pass, and the PR states the speed readings.

Part of #2525 (slice 2 of 6). The maintainer set the priority on 2026-11-18: "GPU shader issues get priority".

Depends on #2612 (the rasteriser) and on the input and spacing types of #2158. The #2158 work is held on `mkinney:issue/2158-nesting-kernel`. Stack on its PR when one is open, or wait for it.

## What to add

A CPU raster candidate search in `camcraft-geometry`, behind an evaluator seam:

- **The evaluator seam.** A trait (or a function value that the caller passes in) with one job: for a sheet raster and a part raster, give the overlap count, or the first legal position, for a set of grid positions. The CPU implementation in this issue is the reference. A later slice (GPU) implements the same seam.
- **The integer evaluation.** Bit-packed AND and `count_ones` over the part rows. Integer arithmetic only. Stop early at the first occupied cell where only a yes or no is necessary.
- **Bottom-left order.** The first legal position is the minimum of a packed key: row, then column, then rotation index. Rotations come from the `rotation_mode` of #2158 (and the grain filter of #2398 when it exists).
- **Coarse to fine.** Search on a coarse grid (1 mm default, a parameter). Refine the found position in a window on a fine grid (0.1 mm default, a parameter), in tiles of 4096 x 4096 cells or less.
- **Exact check.** After each placement, test the inflated part against the placed parts and the usable sheet with `geo2d::Region` booleans. A failure marks the part unplaced with a named reason. It never passes silently.
- **Parts in holes.** Free cells inside a hole of a placed part are free when `allow_parts_in_holes` is true, and occupied when it is false.
- Fixed evaluation budget. No wall-clock limit.
- Provenance: no-fit raster (Mundim, Andretta and de Queiroz, Expert Systems with Applications 81, 2017), raster penetration (Sato et al., EJOR 279, 2019), configuration-space obstacles by correlation (Kavraki, IEEE Trans. Robotics and Automation 11, 1995).

## Notes

- Changes nest geometry: under the safety floor. New algorithm: `effort:max`.
- No new crate edge and no new dependency. Record the seam shape, the default cell sizes and the tie-break key in `docs/decisions/<issue>-<slug>.md`.
- No MCP tool in this issue. The `RunNesting` tool of #2160 uses this kernel later.
- Headless tests only. No GPU.

- Rectangles, L shapes and parts with holes nest with zero overlap of the inflated footprints, checked by `Region` booleans.
- A small part sits inside the hole of a large part when `allow_parts_in_holes` is true, and does not when it is false.
- A raster that is wrong on purpose (a test evaluator that reports a false "free") is caught by the exact check, and the part is unplaced with a named reason.
- Two runs give the same layout. The layout does not depend on the thread count.
- The used sheet length is within a stated margin of the #2158 NFP placer on the same fixtures.

title: Nesting raster 1: conservative bit-packed rasteriser for geo2d regions in camcraft-geometry

labels.name: enhancement

body:
Part of #2525 (slice 1 of 6). The maintainer set the priority on 2026-11-18: "GPU shader issues get priority".

## What to add

Add a CPU module in `camcraft-geometry` (for example `crates/geometry/src/nesting/raster/`) that converts a `geo2d::Region` to a bit-packed grid of cells. This is the base of the raster nest of #2525. It has no GPU code and no wgpu.

- A grid has an origin, a cell size (integer, in `geo2d::SCALE` units) and a width and height in cells. Rows are packed in `u32` words.
- **Over-approximate mode** (for parts): mark each cell that the region touches. A cell that only touches the boundary is marked.
- **Under-approximate mode** (for the usable sheet): mark a cell free only when the full cell is inside the region. Holes of the region are not free.
- Use integer arithmetic on the `geo2d` integer coordinates only. No float enters the decision of a cell.
- Refuse by name: a non-positive cell size, a grid larger than a stated cell limit, a non-finite input, an empty region where one is required.
- One-line provenance comment: scanline polygon fill and conservative coverage, from Bennell and Oliveira (EJOR 2008) and general computer-graphics literature.

## Why

The raster finds nest positions fast. It is only a first filter. A raster "free" result must be a true "free" result: parts over-approximate, the sheet under-approximates (#2525, research comment 2).

## Notes

- No new crate edge, no new dependency, no decision entry for an edge. Record the cell-size default and the cell limit in `docs/decisions/<issue>-<slug>.md`.
- No MCP tool: this is a kernel module with no command.
- Work that changes nest geometry is under the safety floor: `effort:high`.
- Headless tests only. No GPU.

## Done means

Tests in `crates/geometry/tests/` show:
- For squares, a part with a hole, a thin sliver and a rotated part, each point of the region lies in a marked cell (over-approximate), checked on a dense point sample.
- Each free cell of the under-approximate sheet lies fully inside the region (all four corners and the cell centre inside, and no region edge crosses the cell).
- The same input gives the same bits on each run.
- Each refusal names its reason.

"Still" means that he saw this before. No open issue names it. The nearest closed issues are #2181 (stock removal calculated before playback) and #1516 (stock cut only at the end of each move). The first agent that works this issue checks if one of them is the same defect. If it is, reopen that issue with this report and close this one as a duplicate.

## What happens

The simulation runs, but the stock does not change on screen. The user sees no material removed as the tool moves.

## Expected

The stock shown at each playback position is the stock after all moves up to that position. A cut is visible.

## Not known yet

- The build or version. The maintainer did not name it.
- The model, the stock type and the operation types.
- The engine: dexel column engine (default) or the field engine (`CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE=field`, #1168).

1. Reproduce on the latest `main` with a headless test: build a part and a simple pocket, run the stock simulation to the end, and assert that the removed volume is greater than zero and that the drawn stock mesh differs from the initial stock mesh.
2. Find where the chain breaks: the toolpath moves, the removal engine, the mesh update, the draw call. Use `graphify query` first.
3. Check that the fix does not break the carried-stock and rest-material users of the same engine.
4. Pin the fix with a test that fails without it. Add the case to the `camcraft-sim` or app test set, in the lowest crate that provides it.

A stock simulation that shows no removal hides what the program cuts. This is `effort:high` by the safety floor. If the engine itself gives a wrong stock (not only a draw fault), raise the priority to P1 and say so in a comment.

title: LinuxCNC and Tormach probe posts write G10 L20 with positions of the active WCS into a different WCS

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

`onProbeResult` in `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps` (PR #2310) writes the found work offset as:

```
G10 L20 P<SetWorkOffset + 1> X[#5420-#<dev>] Y[#5421-#<dev+1>] ...
```

`#5420`-`#5422` hold the current position in the active WCS. `G10 L20 Pn` sets WCS n so that the current position has the given values in WCS n. When `SetWorkOffset` names a WCS that is not the active WCS, the post writes positions of the active WCS into WCS n. The offset in WCS n is then wrong by the difference between the two WCS origins. A later operation in WCS n cuts in the wrong place. The post shows no message.

`assets/posts/tormach.cps` on `main` has the same pattern (`onProbeResult`, the `G10 L20` block with `#5420`).

## Expected

One of these:

- The post makes the target WCS active (or proves it is active) before it reads `#5420`-`#5422`.
- The post refuses by name a `SetWorkOffset` that is not the WCS of the section.

## Evidence

- Review of PR #2310 (non-blocker 3).
- LinuxCNC G-code reference: `G10 L20` ("the current coordinates become the given values") and the parameters `#5420`-`#5428` (current position in the active coordinate system).

## Done means

- `linuxcnc.cps` and `tormach.cps` write a correct offset when `SetWorkOffset` is not the active WCS, or refuse it by name.
- A test pins the case. If possible, the test reads the program back in an interpreter with two WCS origins.

body:
The maintainer asked for this work, in his own words (2026-11-18):

> when hitting simulation there sh ould be an option to "step" thru to next operation.. so we can check the one relevant

## Problem

The simulation plays the whole program from the first move. A user who wants to check one operation must scrub or wait. There is no way to go to the next operation.

## Wanted

1. The simulation controls have a "next operation" step. It moves the playback position to the first move of the next operation in program order.
2. A matching "previous operation" step. It moves to the start of the current operation, and a second press moves to the start of the one before it.
3. The control shows which operation is current (its name from the tree). A step across a setup boundary, a tool change or a WCS change works the same as a step inside one setup.
4. The stock shown at the new position is correct: it is the stock after all earlier operations. A step must give the same stock as playback to that position. A step never skips a removal.
5. Disabled states: "next" is disabled in the last operation. "previous" is disabled at the start of the first operation. The AccessKit labels and the tooltips say what each button does.
6. A keyboard shortcut for each step, listed in the shortcut help.

## Notes

- The playback position is ephemeral UI state (AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command"), so no undoable command is needed. If a step selects an operation in the tree, that selection goes through `SelectEntity`.
- A skipped or suppressed operation is not a stop. An operation with no toolpath is not a stop.
- UI text: plain English, no G-code jargon. A UI PR needs before and after screenshots in the PR body. Tests assert labels, roles, enabled state and the position, not pixel values (`crates/ui/AGENTS.md`).
- Related: #2587 (the stand-alone simulator window). The same step logic should work there. Keep the operation-boundary lookup in the lowest crate that provides it, so both can use it.

## Done means

- A test shows that "next" from a position inside operation 1 gives the first move of operation 2, and that the stock equals the stock from plain playback to that move.
- Tests for the first operation, the last operation, a tool change and an operation with no toolpath.
- The behaviour tests and the page layout test of the simulation panel pass.

title: Research: GPU shader stock simulation with voxels

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
The maintainer asked for this work, in his own words (2026-11-18):

> Add a GPU shader issue and that is for voxel simulation..

It belongs to the GPU shader group: #2525 (nesting) and #2526 (toolpath generation).

## Question

Can a compute shader (wgpu) run the stock simulation on a voxel grid? The CPU path today is the dexel column engine. Issue #26 plans to retire it.

## Open questions for the research

1. Grid design: dense voxel grid, sparse bricks, or dexel columns on the GPU. Memory per cut volume at the stock sizes that users load. Resolution against the tolerance of the setup.
2. Material removal: a swept tool volume (cylinder, ball, bull-nose, tapered tools from the tool library) removed from the grid in one dispatch for each move or batch of moves. Accuracy at arcs and at 4-axis and 5-axis moves.
3. Read-back: a gouge, collision or rest-material result that must block the post needs the data on the CPU. State the cost and the method (async read-back, a compare against the model, a reduction in the shader).
4. Display: render the grid directly (ray march or surface extraction) without a copy to the CPU. Frame target under 10 ms (see the precalc and cache rule).
5. Backends: wgpu on Vulkan, Metal, DX12 and the browser (WebGPU). Compute support on wasm. A CPU fallback for a machine with no usable GPU. Reference #2424 (a driver freeze on one Radeon): a GPU path needs a timeout guard and a safe fallback.
6. Determinism and trust: the CPU result and the GPU result must agree within a stated tolerance. A GPU result that is wrong gives a silent wrong answer. Name the test that proves agreement (golden grids, a CPU reference).
7. Relation to `camcraft-sim`, to the stand-alone simulator (#2574 sub-issues) and to rest-material for the Adaptive and Pocket operations.

## Done means

- The research answers each question in an issue comment, with sources (published literature only; clean-room rule).
- A recommendation: build, build in part, or do not build, with a measured or cited basis.
- Sub-issues for each accepted slice, each with one `P*`, one `effort:*` and `area:*` labels, and linked under this issue.
- Then this umbrella issue is closed (`issue-claims` skill, research steps).

title: ci: build the extra package formats in follow-up pipelines after a release, then add them to the release page

body:
The maintainer asked for this work, in his own words (2026-11-18):

> we should build things like AUR packages, RPM, DEB and the "non-standard" style of packages- after a release.. once release triggers, that should trigger secondary pipelines focused on all the weird package formats, and then backfill the releases backpage after the fact..

## Problem

`release.yml` builds the core artifacts (zip, installer, wasm site) and some package formats (`aur`, `snap`, `flatpak`) in the same run. A slow or broken package job holds the release run open. A failed package job makes the run red, but the release itself is fine. The v0.24.0 run showed this: the `aur` job was still running after all other jobs were green.

## Wanted

1. `release.yml` publishes the core release first. The core is the zip, the installer and the site. It does not wait for the extra formats.
2. The release start triggers secondary workflows. Each workflow builds one family of formats: AUR, RPM, DEB, snap, flatpak and other non-standard formats.
3. Each secondary workflow attaches its artifact to the existing GitHub release after the fact (backfill). It does not move or re-push the tag.
4. A failed secondary workflow does not change the state of the release. It reports its own failure and can run again for one tag (`workflow_dispatch` with a tag input).
5. The release notes or the download page list each format that is attached. A format that is not attached yet is not listed as available.

## Constraints

- AGENTS.md "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted": a new `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger needs the maintainer's approval. Use `workflow_run` or `workflow_dispatch` started by the release run. Name the trigger in the PR body.
- A secondary workflow on a self-hosted runner must never start from a fork PR (`runners` skill).
- Keep the existing `aur-package.yml` and the `aur`, `snap` and `flatpak` jobs working until their replacement is proven on a real tag. Never test on a published tag. Use a throwaway tag in a fork or `dry_run`.
- Do not change the cut procedure: the cut is complete when the tag is on GitHub and `release.yml` attached the core artifact. Update the `release-cut` and `runners` skills for the new flow (a process change: `Process change: yes`).
- Related: #2590 (ship `camcraft-sim` in the packages).

## Done means

- A release tag starts the core run and the secondary workflows.
- The core release is complete before the first secondary workflow ends.
- Each secondary workflow adds its artifact to the same release and can run again for one tag.
- The `release-cut` and `runners` skills describe the flow.
- A decision file in `docs/decisions/` records which formats are in the first slice and which are later.

title: Machine file: reserved tool numbers (the probe's pocket), so a cutting tool is never given that T number

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## What happens

`add_tool` gives each new tool the lowest unused number from 1 (camcraft-mcp skill: "Assigns the lowest unused tool number in 1-99999"). Many machines keep a fixed pocket for the probe or a tool setter:

- Tormach PathPilot machines: the probe is **T99** by convention.
- A Hurco VMX30U (WinMax): the export on #2566 has `PROBE` as **T1**.
- A FANUC Robodrill (31i-A5): the owner's **T1** is the probe.

On the last two, CamCraft's first cutting tool becomes T1, so a posted program calls the probe for a face or drill operation. Found while making the Robodrill test kit (#2603): its first version faced with T01, and the owner answered "I will not face with my probe!". The kit was renumbered to T12-T15 by hand.

## Expected

- A machine file can name reserved tool numbers, for example `"tooling": { "reserved": [ { "number": 1, "use": "probe" } ] }` (the exact key to be decided).
- `add_tool` and the tool library skip those numbers for cutting tools; a probe tool takes the probe's number.
- `set_tool_number` to a reserved number for a tool of the wrong kind is refused by name (or warned), and verify/post warn when a program calls a reserved pocket for cutting.
- The Tormach machine files reserve T99 (probe); a generic VMC reserves nothing.

## Done means

A test with a machine file that reserves T1 for the probe: the first added end mill gets T2, the probe gets T1, and a program that cuts with T1 is refused by name.

body:
## Goal

Check CamCraft's built-in **Fanuc** post on a real Fanuc control: a **FANUC Robodrill, 3-axis, control 31i-A5**, owned by @vilts, who also checks the Hurco post (#2573). The control has a graphic toolpath check, so each program can be checked before anything cuts.

What the owner uses on this machine: **G05.1 Q1 R1** (AI contour control), **rigid tapping**, and a turret ATC with no tool preload (T and M6 on one block).

## Open questions for the post

1. **Rigid tapping:** the post writes `G84 ... F` with no `M29`. On a 31i, G84 is rigid without M29 only when parameter 5200 bit 0 is set. Does this machine need `M29 S..` before G84? If so: a post option (or the default) that writes `M29 S..`.
2. **Peck cycle:** the post writes `G73` (chip break) for a peck drill, at `R0.` (the part top) after a rapid to Z0. Is G73 the right default, or G83 (full retract)? Should R be 1-2 mm above the top?
3. **G05.1 Q1 R1:** the post does not write it today (#616: G5.1 states no tolerance, so it only names the smoothing request in a comment). Where does the owner put `G05.1 Q1 R1` / `G05.1 Q0` (after the tool change, per operation)? That decides a post option.

## Test kit (graph check only - test tools and holes, do not cut)

Tool numbers are test numbers, T12 face mill, T13 D6 end mill, T14 D6 drill, T15 M6 tap - chosen to stay off T1, the owner's probe ("I will not face with my probe!"). Change them to your own pockets first. Each program's first comment says so.

Posted 2026-11-18 by CamCraft main (v0.24.0 code), built-in Fanuc post, generic 3-axis VMC, metric, part = a 120 x 80 x 12 mm aluminium bracket, G54 = top front-left of the stock.

- `01-two-tools.nc`: face with T12 (D10), outside contour 2 mm deep with T13 (D6): tool change, `G43 H`, G2/G3 arcs.
- `02-peck-drill.nc`: seven holes, D6 drill, peck 3 mm (`G73`).
- `03-rigid-tap.nc`: M6 x 1.0 tap on the same holes (`G84`, no `M29`).

Please report per file: "loaded OK" or the alarm number and line, plus a screenshot if the graph looks wrong.

Done means: the three answers above are recorded here; any change they need is a post option or default with a golden test; the kit loads with no alarm on the 31i-A5.

title: Changing a 3-axis mill's machine kind to lathe (edit_machine) lets turning code post as that mill, with no warning

body:
Found by mkinney's QA run p09 (turning on a mill) and narrowed by a verification run on 2026-11-18, CamCraft main `83867fd7`.

On a plain Tormach 770MX, turning operations are correctly refused at `add_operation`. But after `edit_machine {"general": {"kind": "lathe"}}` on the 770MX, turning operations are accepted and the posted program is lathe code (G7/G18, X as diameter) labelled "Tormach 770MX", with no warning that the machine is a mill with a vertical spindle and no lathe axes.

Workaround: use a lathe machine file. Related: #2580 (turning on a mill, the supported way to come).

Done means: a machine-kind edit that contradicts the machine's kinematics (no lathe X/Z, a milling head) is refused by name, or the program header and verify say plainly that a mill was relabelled as a lathe.

Found by mkinney's QA run p05 (wrapped cylinder) and reproduced by a verification run on 2026-11-18, CamCraft main `83867fd7`.

What happens: on a D50 bar with six blind D5 x 8 mm radial holes, two of them opposite each other, `detect_holes` returns `{"holes":1,"radial_holes":0}` with one hole `entry_z 25, floor_z -25, through: true` - a 50 mm through hole across the solid core.

Not unsafe: generating it is refused (the drill is too short; with a long drill the gouge gate refuses the post, 44-50 mm into the model). The refusal text even suggests "drill it with a longer drill, or in stages from both sides".

body:
Found by mkinney's QA runs (p02, p03, p04, p05, p08) and reproduced on a minimal part by a separate verification run on 2026-11-18, CamCraft main `83867fd7` (= v0.24.0 code). Minimal repro projects and posted programs are kept on mkinney's machines and can be attached.

What happens: `verify` on a program with tilted operations returns `ok: true` with `gate.not_judged: "stock sim did not judge this program: SLOT A180: move 2: posed moves are not modelled by the column engine ..."`, and `post` writes the file. The same slot untilted (`SLOT A0`) is correctly blocked: `move 2 cuts past the finish surface`. The tilted slots cut the same model and post.

Why P1: an unjudged program must not post as if it were checked (Prime Directive: anything the simulation cannot judge is refused or clearly held, never passed silently).

Done means: either the stock sim judges posed (tilted) moves, or a program it cannot judge is held from posting with a named reason (with an explicit user override if that is the design), pinned by a test with a gouging tilted op that is refused.

Found by mkinney's QA runs (p02, p03, p04, p05, p08) and reproduced on a minimal part by a separate verification run on 2026-11-18, CamCraft main `83867fd7` (= v0.24.0 code). Minimal repro projects and posted programs are kept on mkinney's machines and can be attached.

What happens (Tormach 770MX + microARC 4, the documented per-operation `tilt` route of the microARC tester kit, #785): `tilt {a_deg: 180}` is refused ("Tool axis A must be in -90..90 ... for the face opposite the top, use Tool axis A 0 and Tool axis B 180"). G0 A180

title: Flaky test: ui --lib diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level loses its INFO line in a parallel run

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Found during the quick gate of PR #2594 (#2340). The PR does not touch `crates/ui/src/diag.rs`.

## What happens

`diag::tests::diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level` (`crates/ui/src/diag.rs:124`) fails in some full parallel runs of `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`:

```
panicked at crates/ui/src/diag.rs:139:9:
the note is an INFO event: 2026-11-18T21:12:45.153099Z  WARN camcraft_ui: gpu: test adapter failed: no surface - trying the next adapter
```

The captured output has the WARN line, but not the INFO line ("headless: test adapter").

Readings on Linux, 12 cores, `--test-threads=10`, tree `v0.24.0` plus PR #2594:
- Full lib run: 1 failure in 3 runs (the quick gate step `ui suites: lib`; then two clean runs, 1170 passed).
- The test alone (`--exact`): 3 passes in 3 runs.

## Suspected cause (not confirmed)

- `diag::info` is one `tracing::info!` callsite. All UI code and all UI tests use it.
- The test installs its subscribers with `tracing::subscriber::with_default`, which is thread-local.
- `tracing` caches the interest of each callsite for the whole process. Other tests run on other threads at the same time, and a new dispatcher causes a rebuild of the cached interest.
- Thus the INFO callsite can be disabled while this test's "info" subscriber is the default on its thread. The WARN callsite stays enabled, which agrees with the output above.

## Expected

The test passes in each parallel run.

## Possible directions (not tested)

- Run the assertions in a separate process or a test binary of its own, so no other test shares the callsites.
- Call `tracing::callsite::rebuild_interest_cache()` after the subscriber is installed, and before each event.
- Serialize the test with the other tests that emit `diag` lines (a lock, as `snapshot_guard` does for the theme cells in #2373).

## Labels

I cannot set labels (no triage access). Suggested by the precedent of #2373: `bug`, `P3`, `effort:medium`, `area:ui`. Filed by an agent session for a contributor, thus `source:agent` also applies.

Done means: `diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level` passes in repeated full parallel runs of `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`, and the fix says which runs were measured.

title: Research: machine model from a URDF file (for example a Solidcraft assembly export)

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: P8

body:
Part of #2574 (research answer 2).

The maintainer named the Solidcraft route in #2574: "Or use solidcrafts model with the joints defined in the solidcraft file. Either way i guess. if we go the solidcraft route a base model could be generated thru its MCP."

## Recommended in #2574
The contract is a file, not a live MCP call. Solidcraft (MIT OR Apache-2.0) exports an assembly with its joints as URDF (`export` tool, `docs/mcp.md` of tangency-labs/solidcraft). URDF is a public XML format (wiki.ros.org/urdf/XML): links, `revolute` and `prismatic` joints, `origin`, `axis`, `limit`, mesh references. `camcraft-sim` reads only the file and never needs Solidcraft at run time. Without a URDF, the model comes from the `.mch` (#2584, #2591).

## Open design points
1. The `.mch` key that names the URDF and maps each URDF joint to an axis letter.
2. The units and the root frame of the URDF against the machine frame and the `travel` of the `.mch`. Which file wins when the joint limits differ.
3. The mesh formats to read (STL and OBJ readers exist; GLB does not).
4. Refusals: a joint with no letter, a letter with no joint, a closed chain, a mesh that is not found.

## Done means
The design points have answers in comments, and the code sub-issue is filed with a `P*`, `effort:*` and `area:*` label. No hard dependency on Solidcraft is added.

Part of #2574 (research answer 1, option a).

> "That can generate a "loose" model from the machine file. That would means, table, column, axis, head, spindle etc etc. All joints. "Defined" and loosly generated as a generic block and cylinders design."

## Scope
- Add a module `machine_model` in `camcraft-sim`. Its input is plain data of its own (parts, parent, joint kind, axis, travel, spindle body). `camcraft-sim` gets no edge to `camcraft-post`: the caller maps `MachineTree` (#2583) into the input.

Tests pin the bodies and their poses for a 3-axis VMC and the tilt-head example at two axis positions each, the "generated" mark, and the refusal of degenerate input.

Depends on #2583 (for the mapping only; the module can land first with its own types).

body:
Proposal from mkinney (2026-11-18): "Should we formalize our QA swarm in an issue ... so all can track what it is doing? ... It is starting to feel like integration tests."

What exists: since 2026-11-17 mkinney's agents design parts in the latest SolidCraft and make them in the latest CamCraft end to end (design -> project -> operations -> generate -> verify -> post), and write a report per part. Ten parts so far (p01-p10: flange, bracket, stepped block, threaded boss, wrapped cylinder, all-ops mill part, lathe shaft, microARC 4 part, turning on a mill, plasma plate). They found about 100 problems; filed so far: #2437, #2440, #2443, #2578, #2579, #2580.

## Proposal: two layers

1. **Deterministic (in the normal gate, no AI):** every QA part that posts becomes an example-catalog case (#2392, `cargo xtask catalog`): the `.sc`/`.step`, a recorded build script (the MCP/CamScript steps) and the byte-pinned `.nc`. A regression then shows in the normal gate at no AI cost.
2. **Exploratory (agents, on contributors' own machines, NOT in GitHub Actions):** the agents need AI subscriptions and keys, and AGENTS.md keeps secrets off the self-hosted runners. Runs are made visible by:
   - one pinned tracking issue with a comment per run (versions, parts, results, issues filed);
   - the part briefs in the repository (for example `qa/briefs/`), so anyone can read and improve them;
   - a `source:qa` label on every issue a run files.

## When to run

- after each minor cut tag (test what users download);
- after each SolidCraft release, at most daily (the `.sc` import, #2578, broke this way);
- on demand.

## Decisions for the maintainer

- Do passing parts go into the catalog (#2392) as cases, and is the repository the right home for the briefs?
- The `source:qa` label.

body:
Asked by mkinney (2026-11-18): "If we get confused by those terms, then so will users/others. Make sure it is clear in the docs."

Two different things are both called "mill-turn":
- **Live tooling / lathe milling:** a lathe (multitasking turning centre) that also mills with driven tools, often with a C axis and sometimes a Y axis. This is CamCraft's built-in "Mill-turn" machine (loads as "MULTITASKING 5-AXIS").
- **Turning on a mill (part in spindle):** a 3-axis mill used as a lathe - the part turns in the mill spindle, lathe tools sit on the table, one work offset per tool (Tormach RapidTurn style). Not supported yet (#2580).

What to change:
- A short glossary box with both terms in the turning guide (`site/content/guide/operations/operations-turning.md`), the machine documentation, and the `camcraft-mcp` skill's machine list.
- Never use a bare "mill-turn" in docs or UI text without saying which one; the ribbon's MILL-TURNING tab names the live-tooling kind.

Done means: the glossary is in those three places, and a search of the docs for "mill-turn" finds no use that leaves the meaning open.

title: Research: turning on a mill (part in the spindle, lathe tools on the table, one WCS per tool), e.g. Tormach RapidTurn on a 770MX

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Asked by mkinney (2026-11-18), who has a Tormach 770MX: "you can use a 3d mill like a lathe ... You end up using multiple WCS for each tool and put part in spindle". Wording: this is **turning on a mill (part in spindle)**, not live tooling on a lathe (CamCraft's existing "Mill-turn" machine).

## The setup

- The workpiece is held in a collet in the mill spindle and turns (M3/M4 at lathe speeds).
- Lathe tools (turning, facing, grooving, threading, parting) are clamped on the table in a gang row.
- There is no tool change: each tool is selected by switching to its own work offset (G54...G59, G59.1-3, G54.1 Pn) whose origin is that tool's tip relative to the spindle centre line.
- One length offset describes the part in the spindle: collet nose to the end of the stock stick-out (`G43 H<n>` once; the user keeps T255 for it).
- Lathe Z (along the part) is the mill Z; lathe X (diameter) is a table axis toward the spindle centre line.

## What CamCraft does today (QA run p09, main `83867fd7`)

- No way to declare "part in spindle, tools on the table".
- A lathe operation set accepted on a 3-axis mill machine posts lathe code labelled "Tormach 770MX" with no warning (high; filed separately).

## Open questions

1. Machine description: a part-in-spindle mode, tool stations on the table (position, side of the spindle, WCS), the collet nose and the stock stick-out.
2. Operations: reuse the turning operations; what changes in the X sign and spindle direction per side; constant surface speed vs fixed RPM on a mill spindle; feed per rev.
3. Post: a WCS switch per tool, no M6, safe retracts between stations, the one `G43 H` for the stock.
4. Safety checks: tool blocks vs the collet and the part, max spindle RPM with a part in it, chip direction.
5. Sources: Tormach's public RapidTurn documentation (operator manual UM10393, D32901, TD10561); the user's own 770MX tests.

Plan (user): several CamCraft simulations first, then PathPilot Hub, then air cuts, then real cuts - slowly.

What happens: a 2D Contour with tabs and `tab_height` set (for example 1.5 mm) leaves tabs as tall as one stepdown (about 4 mm with a 4 mm stepdown): the tabs start at the next stepdown level, not at `tab_height` above the bottom. No note says the height was changed.

title: Stock page: a cylinder stock always faces Z; the yaw field cannot tilt it

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:sim

labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:high

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat on 2026-11-18:

> when setting up stock using a cylinder you can't change the direction that the cylinder faces. it is along Z. i want it along X or Y or anything in between. there is a "rotation" but i can't seem to figure out what it does.

What happens:

- On the Stock page, the user picks Cylinder stock. The cylinder's axis always stands along Z.
- The page has one rotation field: "Rotation (yaw deg)". Changing it does nothing visible for a cylinder.

What the code does today:

- `StockShape::Cylinder { diameter, height }` in `crates/geometry/src/geometry/stock.rs` builds the mesh along Z. The shape has no axis or direction field.
- The Stock page sends its rotation as a yaw-only quaternion (`quat_from_yaw` in `crates/ui/src/state.rs`). Yaw turns about Z. A cylinder is round about Z, so the field changes nothing for a cylinder. It turns a Box only.
- `SetStock` stores a full rotation quaternion in the stock's `Location`, so the document and the project file can already hold a tilted stock. Only the UI and the meshing follow Z.

Expected:

- The user can set the cylinder's axis to X, to Y, or to any direction between.
- The rotation field does what its label says, or its label says what it does.

Possible workaround today:

- Put a cylinder model in the document, rotate it with MoveModel, and take the stock "From model". This does not help every path: the simulation's field view refuses a stock that carries a rotation (see #2177).

What the work must decide:

- The controls: three axis angles (yaw, pitch, roll) on the Stock page, or an axis picker (Z / X / Y / custom).
- What the field view and the collision checks do with a tilted cylinder stock (#2177 closed one case of this refusal; a tilted primitive needs the same review).
- Wording: rename or explain the current "Rotation (yaw deg)" field.

title: sccache: crates with a build script, and solidcore below them, miss the cache in each new worktree

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Found during the idle-box Linux measurement of #914 (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/914#issuecomment-6991514439). Part of the #900 build cycle work.

## What happens

A fresh worktree with a warm sccache cache reaches its first app test no faster than a build without sccache. On a 12-core Linux box: 274 s with a warm cache, 264 s without sccache. The #900 goal is 3x faster.

`cargo build --timings` of a warm run (282 s wall):
- `solidcore 1.0.1` compiles for 216 s, on the critical path.
- All `camcraft-*` units together take 41 s. The first one starts at 250 s.

`solidcore` is a cache miss in each new worktree:
- The sccache hash key of `solidcore` changes with the worktree (`94ef89da...` in one worktree, `78bb5f5e...` in another). The tree and the flags are the same.
- In the same worktree, `cargo clean -p solidcore` and a rebuild gives a hit in 3 s.

The crates that miss in a new worktree are the crates with a build script, and all crates that depend on them:
- Build scripts: `serde`, `serde_core`, `thiserror`, `num_traits`, `crc32fast`, one `proc_macro2` variant.
- Dependents: `serde_json`, `flate2`, `miniz_oxide`, `rayon`, `spade`, `solidcore`, `solidcore-record`, `solidcore-ops`, `solidcore-step`, `solidcore-convert`, `solidcore-tess`.

The `.rmeta` of these crates is not the same in two worktrees (for example, `libserde-aab1de1362e9bc28.rmeta` has a different md5). This agrees with an `OUT_DIR` below each worktree's own `target/`.

`SCCACHE_BASEDIRS` (sccache 0.18.0) with the two worktree roots does not change this. `serde`, `thiserror` and `solidcore` stay misses.

## Expected

A fresh worktree with a warm cache does not compile `solidcore` again. Each worktree compiles only our own crates (the #900 intent).

## Possible directions (not tested)

- Make the build-script crates give the same inputs in each worktree, so that sccache can hit them.
- Share the compiled dependencies between worktrees in a different way. Note: AGENTS.md forbids a shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
- Make `solidcore` cheaper in dev builds (for example, its `opt-level`), and measure the effect on the suites that use it.

## Environment

Linux (Manjaro), 12 cores, 32 GB RAM, rustc 1.98.0, sccache 0.18.0, `upstream/main` `c605e5687`. At `7cab31eea`, the dev profile, the `solidcore` pin and the sccache code in `xtask/src/exec.rs` are the same.

## Labels

I cannot set labels (no triage access). Suggested: `P7`, `effort:medium`, `area:build`. Filed by an agent session for a contributor, thus `source:agent` also applies.

Done means: a fresh worktree with a warm sccache cache gets a cache hit for `solidcore`, and the time to the first app test is measured and posted against the #914 numbers.

title: Research: a stand-alone camcraft-sim that plays back G-code on a machine model built from the machine file

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Maintainer request, 2026-11-18, in his words:

"We want a simulator. That can generate a "loose" model from the machine file. That would means, table, column, axis, head, spindle etc etc. All joints. "Defined" and loosly generated as a generic block and cylinders design. This could be refined further in the mch file with its own definition language or even point at source .step file to be the "parts". Or use solidcrafts model with the joints defined in the solidcraft file. Either way i guess. if we go the solidcraft route a base model could be generated thru its MCP. In the end. We want simulation right, the ability to playback a G-code file in a stand alone Application called camcraft-sim, which opens a g-code file, takes a mch and a cps files as references for making sure it does what it should be doing. Maybe even the camproj file so we can run it as a verification of sorts."

"It should still run on the same infrastructure of egui, step loader, solidcore etc. etc.. Alot of the basis is already there but it is it's own executable. That could be launched from within camcraft to easily go from "post -> sim" if we wanted to."

This issue is the umbrella for the research. It is not a request for code. It sets no new decision.

Related open issues:
- #2213 Research: open and simulate a G-code file (any .nc).
- #2218 app: simulate and verify external NC programs against setup stock, model, fixtures and machine.
- #2217 gcode: camcraft-gcode crate for RS-274/ISO 6983 3-axis milling.
- #2224 gcode: multi-axis A/B/C, G43.4 RTCP, G93 and forward kinematics.
- #2226 gcode: 2-axis lathe dialects in the turning sim.
- #2228 gcode: Wire EDM ISO and Sodick taper files.
- #928 Split sim: the stock model below, verify above.
- #1973 Machine collision sweeps for two-axis AC trunnion kinematics.
- #655 UI look and feel of SolidCraft.

Open questions for the research (answer each in a comment, then file the sub-issues):
1. Machine model source. Compare three options: (a) a loose model that xtask or the app builds from the machine file (a block or a cylinder for each table, column, axis, head and spindle, joined by the machine joints), (b) a refinement in the machine file with its own small definition language, (c) a STEP file for each part, named in the machine file. State what the current machine file already holds (axes, limits, kinematic chain) and what is missing.
2. SolidCraft route. Can SolidCraft supply the parts and the joints through its MCP interface? What is the file or tool contract? Does it need a licence or a network? This option must not become a hard dependency. State the fallback when SolidCraft is not there.
3. Inputs of the stand-alone program. G-code file (the dialect comes from the post), `.mch` machine file, `.cps` post file (what check does the post give: dialect, word map, unit, WCS slots?), and optionally a `.camproj` file (stock, fixtures, tools, expected toolpath). State what each file is for and what the program reports when one is missing.
4. What "does what it should do" means. List the checks: machine limits and axis travel, collision of the machine parts with the stock, fixture and tool holder, gouge against the model, rapid through the stock, the difference between the G-code result and the project's own toolpath. Mark which checks exist now in `camcraft-sim` and which are new. Each failed check must block with a diagnostic and must not pass silently (Prime Directive).
5. Layering. The program reuses egui, the STEP loader, Solidcore and the sim crates. Name the crate layout: a new binary crate, which `camcraft-*` crates it may depend on, and what moves out of `app` (see #2268 and #929). A new crate edge needs a `docs/decisions/` entry.
6. Launch from CamCraft ("post -> sim"). How does the app start the program and pass the files? Process, command line, or a shared crate window? What happens when the program is missing?
7. Platforms. The binary builds on Windows, Linux and macOS from one source. State the effect on the release artifacts (`release.yml`, packages).
8. Clean room. Use only public sources: machine-tool handbooks, ISO 6983, public kinematics literature, and Autodesk's published user documentation for behaviour only. State the sources.
9. Order of work. Propose a first slice that gives value alone (for example: 3-axis G-code playback on a loose block model with the limit and collision checks) and the later slices (5-axis, STEP parts, SolidCraft route, the project check).

Done means: each question above has an answer in a comment, the sub-issues exist with `P*`, `effort:*` and `area:*` labels, and this issue is closed with a link list.

Not claimed. A `needs-research` issue is worked as research, with no branch and no PR (`issue-claims` skill).

body:
## Request

A built-in post for Hurco mills with the WinMax control, writing **NC/ISO programs** (Hurco's ISNC dialect, the Fanuc-like one), plus a machine file for a typical 3-axis Hurco VMC. Conversational (Hurco's own format) is out of scope.

A machine owner in the community runs a Hurco with **WinMax 09.01.393.30 (May 2019)**, NC/ISO programs only. WinMax simulates the full toolpath on the machine's screen, so each program can be checked at the control before it cuts, like the PathPilot Hub checks for Tormach.

## Clean-room sources (only these)

- Hurco's public WinMax help: the NC programming G-code table (it marks which codes are ISNC, BNC or both), NC M codes, NC part programming principles, NC parameters (support.hurco.com, WinMax Mill help, NC_Programming section).
- Hurco's public WinMax Mill documentation PDF (704-0116-101).
- What the owner's WinMax simulator accepts and shows.
- Never another CAM product's Hurco post or its output.

## What to decide from the docs

- Program start and end words, program number/comment format, units (G20/G21), the safe start line.
- Tool change (`T.. M6`) and length offset (`G43 H..`); does WinMax want a separate tool-length table call.
- Canned cycles available in ISNC (G73, G81-G89 with G98/G99) and their word formats (Q, P dwell units).
- Arcs (I/J/K vs R), work offsets (G54-G59 and the extended set), coolant, spindle words.
- Anything ISNC requires that Fanuc does not, or refuses that Fanuc allows.

## Done means

- A built-in post `Hurco WinMax (NC)` and a machine file.
- Goldens for contour, pocket, drill, peck, tap, two tools, two work offsets; a test that no word outside the documented ISNC set is written.
- One short program per question checked in the owner's WinMax simulator (load without error, the sim path matches CamCraft's), recorded on this issue.
