body:
Asked by mkinney (2026-11-18): "Can you create a p3 doc issue for that tools export. If you can import tools, add that too. I might want to import tools for future tests on hub."

## What a Tormach user has today

PathPilot can export and import its whole tool table as a `.csv` file (Tormach 770MX operator manual UM10587, section 7.6.4 "Import and Export the Tool Table"): **Offsets tab -> Export -> type a name -> save to a USB drive**; **Import** on the same tab loads a `.csv` back. PathPilot Hub has the same Offsets tab.

CamCraft today:
- imports and exports tool libraries only as `.camtools` (`import_tool_library`, `export_tool_library`, #355, #899);
- writes a setup's tool list as a generic CSV for a spreadsheet (`tool_list_export.rs`, #389) - not PathPilot's column layout;
- has no docs page that tells a Tormach user how to get his machine's tools into CamCraft.

So a user re-types every tool (number, diameter, length, description) to make posted programs match the machine.

## What to do

1. **Docs** (site guide, Tormach section): how to export the PathPilot tool table (the steps above), how to bring it into CamCraft, and how the tool numbers map to `T<n>` in the posted program. Same page: the reverse, for PathPilot Hub tests.
2. **Import:** read a PathPilot tool-table `.csv` into the document's tools (or a `.camtools` library): tool number, diameter, length/offset, type and description where the file has them; the user completes what PathPilot does not store (flutes, flute length, holder). One undo step; an MCP tool (or a format option on `import_tool_library`); refuse by name a row it cannot read.
3. **Export (for Hub and the real machine):** write the document's tools as a PathPilot tool-table `.csv` that PathPilot's Import reads, so a Hub test or a real job starts with the same tool numbers and diameters as the posted program.

## Open point

The exact PathPilot CSV columns are not in the manual. mkinney will export his 770MX tool table; that file is the sample to build and pin the parser against (tests with a recorded `.csv`, no machine needed).

Done means: a docs page with the export/import steps; an import that reads the sample file into tools with the right numbers and diameters, pinned by a test; an export that PathPilot Hub imports (checked once in Hub).

title: Contour tabs: the bridge check compares only neighbouring cuts

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

The bridge check in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/tab_bridge.rs` came with PR #2486. It compares only two neighbouring cuts: the cut before a tab and the cut after it.

The check reads only the last `W + D` of the walk before the tab. It reads only the first `W + D` of the walk after the tab. Lead-in and lead-out moves are included.

A different cut can come closer than the tab width. The check does not read that cut. Two cases are known:

- A U-turn of the same ring. A later part of the ring comes near the tab.
- A different ring at the same level.

The reviewer of head `613ba4abf` says that the tab then holds through a strip that is narrower than W. Main had the same limit before PR #2486. The decision file `docs/decisions/2480-tab-bridge-width.md` records this limit.

## Cases seen in the build review (not confirmed as tab necks)

- A 60 x 7 mm inside slot, W = 3 mm, 3 mm tabs. Two cut runs are 2.06 mm apart. The output has no note. The reviewer says the ring is almost a line here, so the distance is across the slot. The reviewer did not confirm a tab neck.
- An inside L-shape with Perpendicular, Arc or Tangential leads. Lead cuts on the two walls of a 14 mm arm come within 0.07 to 3.4 mm of each other. The cuts are in scrap material, far from the tabs. The reviewer says this was present before PR #2486 and is not a bridge failure.

## First step

Write a shape-mask test in `crates/motion/tests/common/shape_mask.rs` (see AGENTS.md, "2D toolpath shape-mask tests"). Use the U-turn case and the second-ring case. Measure the narrowest bridge.

- If no bridge is narrower than the tab width, post the result on this issue. Keep P3.
- If a bridge is narrower than the tab width, raise this issue to P1. AGENTS.md sets P1 for unsafe output.

## Smaller points

- [ ] `SLACK = 1e-6` (`tab_bridge.rs:77`) has no margin for arc chord error. The reviewer found no bridge under W in a probe, but says the margin is small.
- [ ] With a picked start, the windows grow backward only (`tab_bridge.rs:104`, `128-129`). If the first window grows past the pick, the first keep no longer starts at the pick. No note says this. `contour.rs:307-309` then checks `lead_held` on a keep that is not at the pick. The reviewer says this is not a gouge. Add a `tabs:` note, or a refusal by name.
- [ ] No test has more than one tabbed level. The tests in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_bridge.rs` use TAB_H = 1 and a stepdown of 2. The reviewer's probe with three levels gave a correct result. Add a test with more than one tabbed level.

## Done means

- The shape-mask result is posted on this issue.
- Each smaller point is fixed, or has a `tabs:` note or a named refusal, with a test that pins it.

Refs #2480
Found in the reviews of PR #2486.

title: Research: GPU shader toolpath generation for operations (height field, offset and rest-material passes)

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
The maintainer asked for this research on 2026-11-18. It is the second GPU research issue, after #2525 (nesting).

Question: can a GPU shader generate or help to generate the toolpaths of operations?

Open questions for the research:
- Candidates: find which operation steps map to the GPU. Examples: a height field of the model (drop-cutter, tool-offset field), 2D offset by distance field (pocket, contour, adaptive clearing), rest-material and stock removal fields, collision and gouge checks over a grid.
- Accuracy: a grid has a resolution limit. What resolution holds the tolerance of an operation (for example 0.01 mm over a 500 mm part)? Can an exact check with the vector or mesh geometry remove each risk? A toolpath that gouges is the worst failure (Prime Directive).
- Speed: compare with the CPU generators of `camcraft-motion` and `camcraft-cl`. Estimate the gain for each candidate on the large fixtures. Include the cost of the transfer between CPU and GPU.
- Platform: the project builds on Windows, Linux and macOS, and in the browser build (wgpu). Which compute path works on all of them? Issues #2424 and #74 show that GPU drivers fail on some machines. What happens with no GPU or a bad adapter (CPU fallback, refusal with a diagnostic)?
- Determinism: the same input must give the same toolpath and the same G-code on each machine. Do GPU results differ between drivers (float rules)? How do we pin this with golden files in `tests/golden/`?
- Architecture: where does the code live (a new crate, or `camcraft-motion`)? Which dependency would it add? A new `camcraft-*` dependency needs a decision entry. How does the work fit the command model and the stock simulation?
- Relation to the existing simulation: the stock simulation may already use the GPU. Find what exists, and what can be shared.

Done means: comments on this issue answer each question above, with sources. The research ends with a recommendation (use, do not use, or use only as a preview or first filter before an exact CPU result) and the follow-up issues, each with one `P*` and one `effort:*` label. Then close this issue.

Use only published literature and general knowledge (Clean-Room Protocol).

title: Drill: detect_holes takes holes larger than the drill, and generate and verify pass with no warning (the holes come out undersize)

labels.name: P3

body:
## Problem

`detect_holes` on a Drill operation takes holes that are larger than the drill. `generate` and `verify` then pass with no warning, and `post` writes the program. Each such hole is drilled at the drill diameter, so the finished hole is too small. Nothing tells the user.

This is the Drill twin of #1556 (Bore), which is closed.

## Reproduction (main at 983f527bd, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

Part: a plate 120 x 80 x 10 mm with a boss, exported from SolidCraft as STEP. Through holes: two of D6, two of D8, two of D12.

```
import_model   { "path": "platte_zapfen.step", "name": "Platte" }
fit_stock      { "sides": [2, 2, 2, 2, 0, 0] }
add_tool       { "catalog": "DR-0600" }
add_operation  { "kind": "drill", "tool": "DR-0600", "source": "Platte", "name": "Bohren" }
detect_holes   { "name": "Bohren" }        -> "holes": 6, "skipped": []
generate       { "name": "Bohren" }        -> status ok, warnings []
```

The operation holds holes of radius 3, 4 and 6 (D6, D8, D12). The cache has six `deep` cycles and no warning.

## Expected result

One of these, by name:

- `detect_holes` skips a hole whose diameter is not the drill diameter (within a tolerance), and lists it in `skipped` with the reason (for example "D8.000 hole, D6.000 drill"), or
- `generate` refuses the operation by name, or
- the operation gets a warning that names each undersize hole (for a pilot drill, a user can accept it).

## Proposed priority

`P3` by the AGENTS.md table: a wrong part size with no message, and a workaround (pick the holes by hand). The tool path itself does not gouge or collide.

title: 2D Contour tabs: the bridge on the part is tab width minus the tool diameter; a tab width <= D leaves no tab and frees the part

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## Problem

2D Contour tabs are narrower than the "Tab width" that the user sets. At its narrowest section (the centre line of the cut channel) the tab is `tab_width - tool diameter` wide. When the tab width is equal to or less than the tool diameter, no tab stays. The part comes free during the last levels, and no message tells the user.

## Cause

`Ring::tab_keeps` and `Ring::tab_keeps_from_start` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ring.rs`) measure the tab window on the tool-centre ring. At each end of that window the cutter disc removes `D/2` more material along the centre line of the channel. The bridge is thus `tab_width` wide at the part wall, but only `tab_width - D` wide at the channel centre line.

Example: a 6 mm end mill and a tab width of 5 mm. The window on the centre path is 5 mm long. On the channel centre line the cutter removes 3 mm on each side past the window ends. The two cuts overlap by 1 mm (5 - 6 = -1 mm), so the bridge is cut through.

## Expected result

The tab width is the smallest width of the bridge that stays. For this, the window on the centre ring must be `tab_width + D` long.

If a tab cannot stay (for example, the window with the tool diameter is longer than the tab spacing), refuse the operation by name. Do not cut the part free silently.

## Related

- #1565: Verify and the stock sim do not find a piece of stock that the program frees. Thus this defect is not found by verify either.

## Proposed priority

`P1` by the AGENTS.md table: wrong output that passes. A freed part can move into the cutter.

I can make the fix and a test (shape-mask test of the bridge width) in a PR from my fork.

title: Tormach post: a move without an A angle in an indexed operation turns A back to A0 and is not refused

labels.name: bug

labels.name: P1

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What is wrong

In `assets/posts/tormach.cps` on main (after PR #2386), a rapid or linear record that has no A angle gets `a = 0`.
If the indexed operation has an A angle that is not 0, the post writes a `G0` or `G1` block with an `A0` word.
Before PR #2386, the post refused this record.
A turn to A0 in the middle of an indexed operation moves the work under the tool. That can be a collision or a cut in the wrong place.

## Reading (source only, not built, not run)

1. A record with no A gets `a = 0`: `tormach.cps:691-698`. With a section angle that is not 0, the difference is `-aSection`: `tormach.cps:709-713`.
2. `onRapid` (`:1039`) and `onLinear` (`:1046`) call `motionFor(properties, "")`. The empty name skips the refusal at `:715-716`. The move becomes `aNext = {a: 0}` (`:725`).
3. `turnMove` (`:862-910`) writes the block with the `A0` word (`:888`, `:892`, `:895`, `:907-909`).
4. Arcs, probe moves and canned cycles pass a name, and the post refuses them at `:716`.
5. The engine adds A only when the CL record has an A word: `crates/post/src/post/cnc.rs:194-198`. It does not fill A from the section.

## Not confirmed

- It is not confirmed that the toolpath stream can emit a record without an A angle inside an indexed operation whose angle is not 0. If it cannot, the defect cannot occur today, but no test or refusal guards it.
- It is not confirmed that a turn to A0 is the intended reading of such a record.

## Tests

No test was found for a record without A in an indexed section. Checked by name: `tormach_wrapped_a.rs`, `tormach_fourth_axis.rs`, `fourth_axis_pose.rs`.

## Source

The read-only Opus review of the merged PR #2386, and a source reading after it:
https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2386#issuecomment-6972209368

## Done when

- The first step confirms if the stream can emit such a record, with a recorded `.cl` file.
- A record without an A angle in an indexed operation keeps the section angle, or the post refuses it with a diagnostic. It does not turn A silently.
- A test pins the result for a rapid record and for a linear record.

body:
The maintainer asked for this trial on 2026-11-18. His words:

> Lets do an experiment. Change the agents and worker skill setup accordingly.. We use fable for orchestration and coordination. Its work is to resolve stuck processes, and make decisions thru reasoning on complex tasks. Opus can be used for this as well if Fable is not available. Opus is then used for all code changes, actual work, sonnet can be used for simpler tasks that is quick small understandable fixes. None of these processes are actually doing the file handling, haiku is doding all the file readding, finding, locating on the grap creating the context. This means we can have 4 long running haiku agents at all times and the opus/sonnet agents come and go per usual. The orchestration/coordination agent sits as its own agent so we leave mains session open for reporting, taking questiotns and deal with the user.

> Set this up locally first and lets try for a while prepare it as a draft docs PR but flag it held-for-merge right away.

The work:
- Add a `coordinator` agent (Fable; Opus when Fable is not available). It picks issues, dispatches workers, resolves stuck processes and decides.
- Add a `context-scout` agent (Haiku). Four scouts run at all times. They read files, search, query the knowledge graph and write context packs. They change nothing.
- Set the issue workers to Opus. Set the `effort:low` worker to Sonnet.
- Change the `work-issue` skill: a worker gets its context from a scout and does no broad search.
- The main session keeps the user: reports, questions and maintainer decisions.
- State the roles in `AGENTS.md`.

The trial runs from local files first. The PR is a draft with `held-for-merge`.

Done means: the maintainer ends the trial. Then the PR merges, or it is closed with the result in a comment.

title: An unnumbered tool's T/H number is its name-sorted list position, so adding a tool renumbers the others between posts

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

A tool with no number of its own posts as its 1-based position in the document's tool list (`crates/app/src/tool_numbers.rs`, #221), and that list is in name order. Adding a tool whose name sorts earlier renumbers every tool after it. Re-posting the same operations after adding a tool changes the T/H words of tools the operator has already loaded and touched off.

## Evidence (upstream main abe24ff09)

QA project tools, `posts_as` before: CM-1000-90 = 1, DR-0600 = 2, EM-0600-4FL = 3, EM-1000-4FL = 4, SPOT-0600-90 = 5, SPOT-CM-0600-90 = 6. After `add_tool {catalog: "EM-0600-4FL", name: "AA-FIRST"}`: AA-FIRST = 1, CM-1000-90 = 2, DR-0600 = 3, EM-0600-4FL = 4, EM-1000-4FL = 5, SPOT-0600-90 = 6, SPOT-CM-0600-90 = 7. `number` stays null on all of them. In the QA run, adding `SPOT-0600-90` moved `SPOT-CM-0600-90` from T5 to T6.

A program posted before and after the add calls the same end mill T4 and then T5. On a PathPilot table set from the first program, `T5 M6 / G43 H5` loads the old T5 and its length offset: a wrong tool and a wrong Z. The program itself is consistent, so nothing in CamCraft can catch it.

## Expected

A tool's posted number is stable once the tool is in the document: e.g. `add_tool` gives the next free number (and says so), or unnumbered tools keep the number they first posted with, and a post with unnumbered tools says which numbers it assumed.

P3 (not P1): the shift needs a controller table set from an earlier post; the setup sheet and program comments name each T. Raise it if the maintainer reads the re-post case as wrong output.

Found by the QA swarm (SolidCraft v0.44.1 + CamCraft v0.23.0, part p01-flange). Re-checked on upstream main abe24ff09.

**Done means:** adding, renaming or deleting a tool never changes another tool's posted T/H number; pinned by a test that posts, adds an earlier-sorting tool and posts again with the same T words.

title: Through holes drilled to the break-through only: the drill point is not added, so a 118 deg drill leaves a ~0.8 mm lip; break_through is not listed by list_operation_types

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

A through hole drilled with a twist drill only gets the fixed break-through below the part bottom (1.0 mm by default, #1557). The drill's point length is not added, so full diameter never reaches the bottom: with a 6 mm 118 deg drill the point is 3 / tan(59 deg) = 1.80 mm long, the tip stops at z -1 and full diameter ends at z +0.8. Each "through" hole leaves a ~0.8 mm cone/lip at the exit. Generate and verify say ok.

Also: the `break_through` parameter from #1557 is not listed by `list_operation_types` for Drill (its default is `null`, so the field is skipped), so an MCP agent cannot find it; the QA agent reported "no break-through option".

## Expected

For a through hole, the depth puts the full diameter at least the break-through below the bottom: bottom - break_through - point length (from the tool's tip angle and diameter), or a stated choice between "tip" and "full diameter"; and `list_operation_types` lists `break_through`.

## Repro (MCP, upstream main abe24ff09)

**Part (p01-flange):** 6061 plate 100 x 60 x 10 mm centred on the origin (z 0..10), a 60 x 30 x 5 mm island on top (z 10..15, R5 corners) with a 1 x 45 deg chamfer on its top edges, 4 x dia 6 through holes at (+-42, +-22), a 10 mm wide x 3 mm deep slot across the +X end (x 35..45, floor z 7). Stock: box fitted to the model with +2 mm on top (100 x 60 x 17, z 0..17). WCS G54 at the stock's min-X min-Y top corner, world (-50, -30, 17). Machine Tormach 770MX, post Tormach PathPilot.

`add_tool {catalog: "DR-0600"}` (D6, tip_angle 118); `add_operation {kind: "Drill", tool: "DR-0600", source: "flange", params: {cycle: "peck", peck: 2}}`; `detect_holes`; `generate`; `post`.

Posted (WCS Z0 = world 17): `G73 X8 Y8 Z-18 R-2 Q2 F300` - Z-18 = world -1, one break-through below the bottom, with no point length.

P3: wrong output a user hits (holes not through at size, burr ring at the exit, verify silent), with a workaround (state a larger break_through by hand). Not a gouge.

Found by the QA swarm (SolidCraft v0.44.1 + CamCraft v0.23.0, part p01-flange). Re-checked on upstream main abe24ff09.

**Done means:** a through hole's posted depth takes the drill point into account (or offers that choice), the sim shows a clean exit, `list_operation_types` lists `break_through`, and a test pins Z for a 6 mm 118 deg drill on a 10 mm plate.

title: MCP generate with no name leaves the operations after an edited one stale

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

`generate` with no name is documented as regenerating "every operation that is not current". After an upstream operation is edited, one call regenerates only that operation; the operations after it **become stale as a result** and are left stale. A second call is needed (the QA run on v0.23.0 needed three). `generate`'s reply lists only what it regenerated, and `verify` then answers `"skipped": "an operation is stale or never generated - regenerate before judging the program"`.

## Expected

One `generate` with no name leaves every operation current: it regenerates in program order and includes the operations that went stale because an earlier one changed.

## Repro (MCP, upstream main abe24ff09)

On the QA project (Face, Island Adaptive, Outside Contour, End Slot, Spot, Peck Drill, Island Chamfer - all ok):

1. `set_operation_area {operation: "Island Adaptive", area: {extension: 6}}`
2. `generate {}` -> `generated: [Island Adaptive]`
3. `get_job` -> Outside Contour, End Slot, Spot, Peck Drill, Island Chamfer are all **stale**
4. `generate {}` -> regenerates those five.

(An edit that does not change the stock the later operations see, e.g. Adaptive stepover 3 -> 3.1, does not show it.)

P3: the tool does not do what it says and an agent cannot tell from the reply that work is still stale; workaround: call it until it returns `[]`. Check whether the GUI's Generate All shares the loop.

Found by the QA swarm (SolidCraft v0.44.1 + CamCraft v0.23.0, part p01-flange). Re-checked on upstream main abe24ff09.

**Done means:** after an upstream edit, one `generate` with no name leaves no operation stale (a test asserts every op's status after the single call), and the MCP description matches.

title: 2D Adaptive in a zero-margin stock leaves 5 mm posts at the stock corners with an ok verdict, and area extension cuts into the island instead

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

A 2D Adaptive on a whole model, in a stock fitted with no XY margin, has to clear the stock above the plate (z 15..10) around the island. Two linked problems:

1. **Corner posts, no finding.** The round tool is kept inside the stock outline as if it were a wall, so it never reaches the four sharp stock corners. Four ~5 mm posts stay at the corners (`render_stock`: rest max 5.0 at (-49.8, -29.8, 15), 113.9 mm3 after the whole program). Nothing later in the program removes them (the contour runs outside the plate). `generate` and `verify` both say ok; the posts only show as amber in `render_stock`. The posted program leaves material the model does not have.
2. **The extension meant for this cuts into the island.** `set_operation_area {extension: 6}` (documented as "extend past exterior edges") also pushes the **island** boundary inward: `gouge: program cuts below the model in 2432 cell(s), worst 5.00 mm at (-26.56, -13.44, z 10.00)`, 4667 mm3. Verify blocks the post (the gouge law of #1603 holds), so it is caught, but the one control that should reach the corners is unusable on a part with an island.

## Expected

The stock outline of a whole-model clearing is an open side the tool may pass over (or the extension grows only the exterior/stock edges, never an island), so the corners are cleared to the floor; and if material above the model is left, the op says so.

## Repro (MCP)

**Part (p01-flange):** 6061 plate 100 x 60 x 10 mm centred on the origin (z 0..10), a 60 x 30 x 5 mm island on top (z 10..15, R5 corners) with a 1 x 45 deg chamfer on its top edges, 4 x dia 6 through holes at (+-42, +-22), a 10 mm wide x 3 mm deep slot across the +X end (x 35..45, floor z 7). Stock: box fitted to the model with +2 mm on top (100 x 60 x 17, z 0..17). WCS G54 at the stock's min-X min-Y top corner, world (-50, -30, 17). Machine Tormach 770MX, post Tormach PathPilot.

`add_tool {catalog: "EM-1000-4FL"}`; `add_operation {kind: "2D Adaptive", tool: "EM-1000-4FL", source: "flange", params: {top_z: {reference: "top_of_model", offset: 0}, bottom_z: {reference: "bottom_of_model", offset: 10}, stepdown: 5}}`; `generate`; `verify` (ok, no finding) and `render_stock` (amber corner posts). Then `set_operation_area {operation: <it>, area: {extension: 6}}`, `generate`, `verify`.

## Evidence

- Upstream main abe24ff09: the saved project verifies `ok: true`, findings `[]` with the corner posts in place. With `extension: 6` verify gives blocking `gouge` findings from move 253 on (the QA run's numbers on v0.23.0 are quoted above).
- Workaround: give the stock an XY margin larger than the tool radius, or a separate op for the corners.

P3: wrong output a user hits (material left above the model with an ok verdict; the documented control refused), with a workaround; the gouge itself is caught by verify. Related: #1603 (the extension gouge is refused there by design - this asks that it not be generated), #1554, #1565.

Found by the QA swarm (SolidCraft v0.44.1 + CamCraft v0.23.0, part p01-flange). Re-checked on upstream main abe24ff09.

**Done means:** on this part, a whole-model 2D Adaptive in a zero-margin stock clears the stock corners to its Bottom Z (or names the material it leaves), and `extension` grows only the exterior boundary - the island stays untouched and verify is clean. Pinned by tests on an island-on-plate part.

title: 2D Contour on a whole model stops where the part grows outward below Top Z (chamfer, slot floor): Bottom Z, step-downs and tabs are dropped with no finding

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

A 2D Contour on a whole model (no picks) takes its ring from the part's section at Top Z and walks it only while the wall it trims stands at the same place (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_depth.rs`). When the part grows outward below that plane - a chamfer, a step, a slot floor - the ring stops there. Bottom Z, the step-down ladder and the tabs below that level are dropped with no note: generate says ok, verify says ok, and the "outside contour" leaves the part attached and its sides unfinished.

Two cases on the same part:

1. **Default Top Z (top_of_model, z 15):** the section at z 15 is the island's top face, so the contour runs **one loop around the island at Z-2 (z 15) only** - no step-downs, nothing on the plate outline, no tabs, though Bottom Z is -0.5 and tab_count 4. (The island widens below z 15 because of its chamfer, so the ring stops at once.)
2. **Top Z = bottom_of_model + 10 (plate top):** the section at z 10 includes the open slot notch. The ring runs Z-7, Z-9, Z-10 (z 10, 8, 7) and stops at the **slot floor** (z 7), where the plate outline closes. The plate sides from z 7 down to -0.5 are never cut and no tab move is written.

## Expected

The outside profile of the part from Top Z down to Bottom Z (-0.5), with the 4 tabs in the bottom 1.5 mm - each level using the part's outline at that level - or, if a ring cannot go deeper, a finding that names the level it stopped at and why (the Prime Directive: mark it incomplete rather than post a silently partial path).

## Repro (MCP)

**Part (p01-flange):** 6061 plate 100 x 60 x 10 mm centred on the origin (z 0..10), a 60 x 30 x 5 mm island on top (z 10..15, R5 corners) with a 1 x 45 deg chamfer on its top edges, 4 x dia 6 through holes at (+-42, +-22), a 10 mm wide x 3 mm deep slot across the +X end (x 35..45, floor z 7). Stock: box fitted to the model with +2 mm on top (100 x 60 x 17, z 0..17). WCS G54 at the stock's min-X min-Y top corner, world (-50, -30, 17). Machine Tormach 770MX, post Tormach PathPilot.

- `add_tool {catalog: "EM-1000-4FL"}`
- Case 1: `add_operation {kind: "2D Contour", tool: "EM-1000-4FL", source: "flange", params: {bottom_z: {reference: "bottom_of_model", offset: -0.5}, stepdown: 3.5, tab_count: 4}}`, `generate`, `verify`, `post {post: "Tormach PathPilot"}`
- Case 2: same with `top_z: {reference: "bottom_of_model", offset: 10}, stepdown: 2, tab_count: 4, tab_width: 6, tab_height: 1.5`

## Evidence (upstream main abe24ff09)

Case 1 - the whole operation:
```
G0 X83.216 Y11.178 Z0
G1 X83.216 Y11.178 Z-2 F300
G1 X25 Y10.999 Z-2 F1200
G2 X15.999 Y20 Z-2 I0 J9.001
...
G0 X67.225 Y10.655 Z25
```
(X15.999..84.001, Y10.999..49.001 = the island top outline offset by r 5; one level only.)

Case 2 - three levels, deepest Z-10 (world z 7, the slot floor):
```
G1 X89.443 Y-4.801 Z-7 F300   ... loop with the notch G2 X90 Y60 / X95 Y65 ...
G1 X89.443 Y-4.801 Z-9 F300   ...
G1 X89.443 Y-4.801 Z-10 F300  ...
G0 X77.479 Y-5.695 Z25        (end of op)
```
Bottom Z is world -0.5 (WCS Z-17.5). Verify: ok, no finding. The stock in this run has no XY margin, so nothing flags the uncut sides; with real oversized stock the part stays attached.

**Priority P2, not P3:** it does not gouge, but it is the default whole-model 2D Contour silently ignoring a stated Bottom Z and tabs, with no diagnostic anywhere (generate, verify, post) - the op posts a partial program as complete. Not P1 because it removes less, never more.

Found by the QA swarm (SolidCraft v0.44.1 + CamCraft v0.23.0, part p01-flange). Re-checked on upstream main abe24ff09.

**Done means:** on this part both cases contour the plate outline down to Bottom Z with the tabs written (or each ring that cannot go on is refused/flagged by name with the level it stopped at); pinned by tests on a part whose outline grows below Top Z (chamfered island, open-ended slot floor).

body:
## What happens

A 2D Chamfer with no picked edges, on a model whose edge already carries the modelled chamfer, puts the cone tip on the **top** edge of the chamfer (the top face's outline) and drops it by the width. The tip runs 1 mm inside the island wall. The posted G-code cuts a V into the part, and `verify` says `ok: true`, gouge 0. In the QA run `render_stock` painted the chamfer band as uncut rest, so the sim is not judging the cone that is posted (the edge-break credit appears to accept it as the intended break).

## Expected

Either the chamfer's lower edge (the wall at y = -15, z = 14) is the edge the cone rides, giving tip (y -15, z 14) and the modelled 1 x 1 chamfer, or the op refuses / says the edge is already chamfered. In any case verify must convict a cone that cuts below the model.

## Repro (MCP, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

**Part (p01-flange):** 6061 plate 100 x 60 x 10 mm centred on the origin (z 0..10), a 60 x 30 x 5 mm island on top (z 10..15, R5 corners) with a 1 x 45 deg chamfer on its top edges, 4 x dia 6 through holes at (+-42, +-22), a 10 mm wide x 3 mm deep slot across the +X end (x 35..45, floor z 7). Stock: box fitted to the model with +2 mm on top (100 x 60 x 17, z 0..17). WCS G54 at the stock's min-X min-Y top corner, world (-50, -30, 17). Machine Tormach 770MX, post Tormach PathPilot.

1. `add_tool {catalog: "CM-1000-90"}` (90 deg taper, D10)
2. `add_operation {kind: "2D Chamfer", tool: "CM-1000-90", source: "flange", params: {width: 1}}` - no picks
3. `generate`, `verify`, `post {post: "Tormach PathPilot"}`

## Evidence (upstream main abe24ff09, same as v0.23.0)

```
G0 X75 Y15.999 Z25
G1 X75 Y15.999 Z-3 F300
G1 X25.05 Y15.999 Z-3 F1200
```
WCS Y15.999 / Z-3 is world y = -14.001, z = 14. The island wall is at y = -15; the chamfer surface runs from (y -15, z 14) to (y -14, z 15). A 90 deg cone with its tip at (-14, 14) reaches 0.71 mm normal into the chamfer face (it cuts a ~2 x 2 chamfer with a V below the modelled one). With `width: 0.5` the XY stays at Y15.999 and only Z changes (Z-2.5), so the width never moves the ride off the top edge.

`verify` on the same program: `ok: true`, findings `[]`, gate ok.

Workaround seen by the QA run: pick the chamfer's lower edge chain (z = 14) with `set_operation_geometry`; that posts `Y15 Z-3`, which is correct, and the sim is clean. `set_operation_area {offset: 1}` is refused ("a 2D Chamfer's cone lies on the picked wall - its ride cannot be offset or clipped").

Priority P1: posted G-code that cuts into the part and passes verify (Prime Directive). Related: #303, #529, #1891 (edge-break records and their credit).

Found by the QA swarm (SolidCraft v0.44.1 + CamCraft v0.23.0, part p01-flange). Re-checked on upstream main abe24ff09.

**Done means:** the no-pick 2D Chamfer on a model with a modelled chamfer either rides the chamfer's lower edge (tip at the wall) or refuses by name; and a chamfer cone that cuts below the model is a blocking verify finding, not edge-break credit. Pinned by a test on this geometry (tip XY/Z asserted, verify verdict asserted).

body:
Asked for by Mike (collaborator) on 2026-11-18, after a Windows 11 user's "it kept crashing" report: "We should add some/most of that in a FAQ or Windows Troubleshooting on CamCraft docs for Windows users."

A new page in the user guide (site/content/guide/, linked from the install page and the FAQ), plain language:

1. **The app does not start or closes at once:** start it with another graphics backend - a shortcut with `--gpu-backend dx12`, `vulkan` or `gl` added to Target. What each means, in one line each.
2. **The whole PC freezes, the screen shows "snow"** (seen on a desktop Ryzen 5 with onboard Radeon): this is a graphics driver or hardware hang that CamCraft's 3D view triggers, not a CamCraft crash. Checks, in order: the latest AMD/Intel/NVIDIA driver from the vendor's site; onboard graphics use main RAM, so try the BIOS RAM profile (XMP/EXPO) off and set "UMA Frame Buffer Size" to 2-4 GB; BIOS update; temperatures.
3. **Testing the PC itself:** free tools by name and what each tests - MemTest86 (RAM, from USB), OCCT (CPU/RAM/graphics with temperatures), HWiNFO64 (temperatures). Note: save work first.
4. **What to send us:** `dxdiag` -> "Save All Information" (note it contains the PC name), the CamCraft log file and where it is (once #2421 lands), the version, and the step where it failed. Where to send it (GitHub issue or Discord).
5. **Windows on ARM / virtual machines:** the x64 build runs under emulation; it worked on a Parallels ARM VM using the software renderer, slower.

Done means: the page exists in the guide, is linked from the install page, and builds with `zola build`. No claims we have not tested; tools are named, not endorsed.

title: Windows crash reports carry no diagnosis: the chosen GPU adapter/backend goes to stdout only, never to the log file

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
A Windows 11 user reported that v0.23.0 "kept crashing" and uninstalled it. We had nothing to go on: no log, no GPU, no step.

A check on a second Windows 11 machine (Intel Arc 140T + NVIDIA RTX 5050 laptop, v0.23.0 zip) found the app runs there with the default, dx12 and vulkan backends, so the crash is likely tied to the user's GPU/driver. It also found:

- The adapter/backend line ("gpu: using/adapter ...") is printed to **stdout only**. It is not in the log file. A user who launches from the Start menu and sends us their log cannot tell us which GPU path crashed.

Wanted (smallest useful set):
1. The chosen adapter (name, vendor, driver, backend) and the list of adapters found are written to the log file at startup.
2. A panic, or a wgpu device/surface error at startup, is written to the log file with its message and a backtrace, before the process exits.
3. The log file's location is easy to find (e.g. named in the About/Help dialog, or printed in the crash message).
4. If startup fails on one backend, the error says which `--gpu-backend` values to try.

Done means: launching on Windows without a terminal leaves a log file that names the adapter and backend, and a forced startup failure (e.g. `--gpu-backend` set to a backend the machine lacks) leaves its error in that log. Pinned by a test of the log setup where it can be tested headlessly.

body:
Split out of #2389 (P1). The generation side of #2389 is fixed on `issue/2389-tilt-heights-axis`: a tilted operation's reference heights (Top/Bottom of stock, Top/Bottom of model, Work offset) are now read along the turned tool axis (`camcraft_app::operation::fold_height`). The display was not changed there.

What still happens (from #2389's investigation):
- `crates/ui/src/interact.rs` `height_planes` / `height_plane_lines` draw the Clearance/Retract/Top/Bottom planes as horizontal rectangles at the setup Z, across the stock's XY box. They do not read the tilt.
- `crates/ui/src/operations.rs` `height_echo` prints "(= Z ...)" from `resolve_height`, the setup-Z resolve. For a tilted op on an asymmetric stock this number is not the value generation uses.
- `operation::region_z` (used by `interact.rs`, `boundary_viz.rs`, `boundary_draft.rs`) also reads the setup Z for a tilted op.

Expected: for a tilted op, each plane stands at right angles to the tool axis, at the distance `fold_height(...) - origin.z` along it from the plane origin, over the stock's extent in the plane's local XY (`TiltedFrame::to_world`). The echo states the value along the tool axis (e.g. "(= 5.000 along tool axis)") from the same `fold_height` call generation makes.

Repro: `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj`, "Flat A90" > Heights tab (the planes lie flat above the bar). On that symmetric bar the numbers agree; on an asymmetric stock (#2390) they do not.

Done means: the viewport planes and the "(= ...)" text of a tilted op use the op's frame and `fold_height`; a ui law test pins a tilted plane's corners and the echo value on an asymmetric stock; untilted planes and text unchanged.

4. A name is stable while the model does not change. The same item has the same name on each page.
5. The table is derived data. It is calculated one time for each model change and cached, not on each frame.

body:

> Issue, needs-research; Router specific milling. Might need its own tabb, like milling, turning etc. But holds functions like Nesting, Grain matching, multiple spindle drill heads and so on.. This is what we need to research.. What is popular for example check cloudcuts capability that is specifically targeting routers.

This is a research issue. It gets no code, no branch and no PR. The research answers the questions in comments and files the sub-issues.

**Questions**
1. Which functions do the popular CAM products for CNC routers have that a milling CAM does not have? Make a list with one line for each function.
2. What does CloudCuts offer for routers? Use only its public pages and public documents. Record behaviour only.
3. Which other router products are popular? Examples to check: nesting-based sheet products for cabinet work and sign work. Name each source.
4. Nesting: the research and the sub-issues are in #2156 and #2158 to #2166. What do those issues not cover for a router workflow?
5. Grain matching: how does a user state the grain direction of a sheet and of a part? How does the nesting obey it? How does a product keep the grain continuous across adjacent parts?
6. Multiple-spindle drill heads (drill blocks, gang drills): how does a machine file describe the spindles and their offsets? How does a post select one or more spindles for a hole pattern? Which controls and which G-code or M-code words are public?
7. Other router functions to judge: tabs and onion skin, small-part hold-down order, vacuum zones, sheet labels, remnants, dogbone and T-bone corners, tool changes on an aggregate head.
8. Does CamCraft need a Router tab beside Milling and Turning? Or does a machine type that shows and hides operations on the Milling tab do the work? Give one recommendation and the reason.

**Rules for the research**
- Clean-Room Protocol: use public documentation and published literature only. Do not copy text, UI strings, names or images of a product.
- The machine research in #1907 and #1918 has router controller data. Link it, do not repeat it.
- Each proposed function gets one sub-issue with `source:agent`, one priority, one effort label and its area labels.

Done means:
- Each question has an answer in a comment, with its public sources.
- The sub-issues are filed and linked here.
- The decision on the Router tab is put to the maintainer as one question.
- Then this issue is closed.

title: Machine file: name the post that writes its programs, and offer it when the machine is mounted

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: area:post

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
### What are you trying to do

I picked the shipped grblHAL machine for a setup that posted with Fanuc. The setup kept Fanuc, and nothing suggested the grblHAL post. A `.mch` file cannot say which post goes with it. `post_offer` offers `default_post_for(kind)` only when the current post does not serve the machine's kind, so for every mill the offer is Fanuc. The pairings exist only as comments in `MACHINES`. #1915 and #1918 expect `default_post_for` to map machines to their post, but it takes only the kind.

### How you imagine it working

- An optional key, for example `controller.post: "grblHAL"`, names a post in `BUILTINS`. Without the key, nothing changes.
- `validate_text` refuses, naming the key, a name not in the registry and a post that does not serve the machine's kind.
- When the mounted machine names a different registry post than the setup's, the existing offer banner suggests the named post. Taking it goes through the existing undoable post command. A mount still never changes the post by itself, and a `.cps` file post is never offered over (#343, #388).
- The shipped machines whose pairing is already written down state their post (Tormach, grblHAL/Sienci, TinyG, Makera, Doosan, Haas, the sinker template). The generic ones state none. `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the key.
- `Machine` is `#[serde(default)]`, so an older reader drops the field. That loses only the offer, never a posted program, so I propose no `PROJECT_VERSION` bump.

Question: should this live in the `.mch` file or in a table next to `MACHINES`? I'd choose the file, so a user's own machine can state its post too. Either way it should fit #924's registry move.

**Tests:** grblHAL mounted over Fanuc offers grblHAL, and taking the offer then undoing it restores Fanuc. A machine without the key offers as now, with the existing lathe-over-mill test unchanged. A `.cps` post is never offered over. The validator refuses an unknown name and a post of the wrong kind. Every shipped machine validates.

Not in scope: a `.cps` path in the machine file, or post options in the machine file.

Related: #1915, #1918, #924, #611. I'd like to claim this and open a draft PR once it is triaged.

  law_tests::gizmo_tests::a_moved_origin_shows_axes_and_triad_together
  law_tests::gizmo_tests::each_triad_is_labelled_with_its_own_offset_name

  law_tests::path_tests::the_path_wears_the_colour_vision_palette_and_off_restores_it

  law_tests::preview_tests::selecting_an_operation_outlines_its_cut_region
  path_lines::tests::the_mark_follows_the_colour_vision_palette_and_the_dim

Suspected mechanism:

The suite mutates process-global cells in parallel frames while
colour-scan law tests read them. Candidates:

- theme::set_current / theme::current: a live OnceLock RwLock, one cell per
  process (crates/ui/src/egui_app/theme.rs); state.rs writes it on each

process-global theme / colour-vision cells with snapshot_guard(), or
serialise those suites. Then pin it with repeated parallel runs (goal:
0/30 failures across repeated full parallel runs).

  (>= 3 runs, 0 failures each).

title: grblHAL and Tormach posts write G86 with no P when the bore dwell is 0

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
What happens: The grblHAL and Tormach posts write a G86 block with no P word when the bore dwell is 0 (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps` and `assets/posts/tormach.cps`, `onCycle`). Each new G86 block comes after G80.

The LinuxCNC interpreter requires P on the first G86 block of a cycle. `src/emc/rs274ngc/interp_cycles.cc`, `convert_cycle_xy`:

```
CHKS(((settings->motion_mode != G_86) && (block->p_number == -1.0)),
    NCE_DWELL_TIME_P_WORD_MISSING_WITH_G86);
```

The LinuxCNC G-code reference gives the format `G86 ... R- L- P- $-` and lists "a P number is required" as a canned-cycle error. grblHAL follows the LinuxCNC specification for its canned cycles.

Expected: A bore with a dwell of 0 posts a program that the control accepts. One option is `P0` on G86 (the LinuxCNC reference permits a P that is not negative). Check the grblHAL code list for G86 first.

Priority: `P3`. The control stops the program with an error. The output is not a silent wrong motion. The behaviour on a real grblHAL or PathPilot control is not verified.

Evidence: Found during the work on #2360. The G86 goldens of `crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs` (grblhal, tormach) show G86 with no P.

Done means: A test pins the G86 P word for a zero dwell on the two posts, and the goldens agree.

Siemens, *SINUMERIK ONE / 840D sl / 828D ISO dialects*, Function Manual, 07/2021, section 6.3, table 6-2 (drilling cycles, ISO dialect M) gives the address words of each cycle. Two cycles in `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps` (`onCycle()`) do not agree with it:

- G84 (tapping): the table lists a P word. The post drops a G84 dwell and gives no warning (`g !== "G84"`).
- G85 (ream, `REAM`): the table lists no P word. The post writes `P<ms>` on G85 when the dwell is above 0.

The G86 dwell refusal agrees with the table (no P on G86). G82 and G89 agree (P listed).

## Expected

- G84: the post writes the P dwell, or it refuses the dwell by name with `msg()`. It never drops it silently.
- G85: the post refuses a dwell by name, or it gives a source that shows P on G85.

## Notes

- Do not change behaviour without a source. Use behaviour only from the manual; do not copy its text.
- Check first if the stream can give a TAP or REAM cycle with a dwell above 0.
- Found during #2349 / PR #2353.

body:
Found while writing the continuous 4-axis walkthrough for #1904 (stacked on PR #2342, which posts wrapped A on `tormach.cps`).

**What happens.** A Rotary Offset rough on the microARC 4 machine file does not post once a level meets the part:

```
post blocked - 1 warning(s): A361.862 in operation Journal is beyond the A axis travel -360..360 degrees - A counts on through 360 (PathPilot does not roll A over), so the operation turns too far in one direction
```

**Why.** `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_offset.rs` develops the bar as a cover of two laps plus the seam pad ("the cover is two laps, the seam copy included"); only an air level sweeps one lap. PathPilot does not roll A over (Hub reading 1 on #796), so the post counts A on, and the machine file states A travel -360..360 (kept in PR #2342: "PathPilot's real A limits are an open Hub check"). Two laps plus the pad cannot fit in 720 degrees.

**Repro (on the #1904 branch, before the demo was changed to Rotary Parallel).** 3/4 in round bar as stock (a model, R 0.375 in, X-1.5..0), a stepped model (journal R 0.340 in), 1/8 in ball, Rotary Offset with radial stepdown 0.03 in, any strategy (Auto, Zigzag, Waterline, Offset rings; climb or conventional): each is refused with A between 360.9 and 363.4. With a Box stock and a 0.1 in stepdown the only level is an air level (one lap, A-86.25..273.75) and it posts, but it cuts nothing.

**Expected.** One of:
- the rough's rings close without a second lap (or each ring unwinds: lift, turn A back, go on), so a level stays inside 720 degrees; or
- the machine file states the travel PathPilot really allows, if the Hub check of PR #2342 (step 5) shows it is wider; or
- the refusal says what to change.

**Workaround.** None found: Rotary Offset cannot be used on this machine file today. Rotary Parallel posts (its A stays inside one turn).

Done means: a Rotary Offset rough of a round bar posts on `tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch` with `tormach.cps`, pinned by a test, or the limit is documented with a refusal that names the fix.

title: Rotary Parallel finishes both end faces of the model to the axis: on a bar held in a chuck that is a cut through the bar, and no setting limits it

labels.name: bug

labels.name: claimed

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max

body:
Found while writing the continuous 4-axis walkthrough for #1904 (Tormach 770MX + microARC 4, stacked on PR #2342).

**What happens.** Rotary Parallel lays the bar down and runs the finishing raster over the whole model, end faces included (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary.rs`, `rotary_parallel`). Each end face is finished down to the fitted axis. On rotary work the bar is held at one end (chuck) or both (chuck and centre), so the chuck-side "end face" of the model is inside solid bar. The pass there is a groove one tool diameter wide, cut from the skin to the centreline: it parts the bar.

**Evidence.** `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` on the #1904 branch: a cylinder model 0.680 in across from X-1.25 to X0, a Box stock from X-2 to X0, a 1/8 in ball tool. The posted program (`examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc`) feeds the tool tip at X-1.3125 down to Z-0.029 (Z is the radius from the A centreline), with the stock box going on to X-2. Pinned by `continuous_4axis_part::the_pass_cuts_the_chuck_side_end_face_to_the_centreline`.

What stops it today, and what does not:
- A tool whose flute is shorter than the depth is blocked at post: "shank/holder at move N collides with the uncut stock" (pinned by `a_short_flute_is_blocked_at_the_chuck_side_end_face`, 1/2 in flute). Good.
- A tool with a long enough flute (5/8 in here, or the catalog `BN-0600` default of 15 mm) posts with no warning.
- No setting keeps the pass off an end face. **Bottom Z** is a floor in the laid frame, not a radius: at 0 it keeps only the half of the bar within about 81 degrees of the top and still cuts the end faces to the axis. **Top Z** / **Clearance Z** are radii for the links. There is no axial window (Rotary Contour and Rotary Offset read heights as stations; on a bar lying flat those are inert).
- The kit golden of PR #2342 (`wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc`) has the same shape: its stock ends where its model ends, so CamCraft sees air where the real bar goes on into the jaws.

**Expected.** A way to finish the turned surface only: an axial window (from/to stations along the fitted axis), or an option to leave the end faces, so the pass stops at a shoulder. Until then, a named warning or refusal when an end-face pass enters stock that goes on past the end of the model.

**Workaround.** None for a real cut on a held bar. The #1904 guide page runs the program as an air cut only and says why.

Priority note: filed as P3 (wrong behaviour with no silent gouge of the part: the stock is cut, the model is not). The maintainer may read "parts the bar off with no warning" as P1.

Done means: a Rotary Parallel job on a bar that goes on past the model's chuck-side end either leaves that end face alone by a setting, or is refused or warned by name; a test pins it; the #1904 guide page drops its "air cut only" limit.

title: Post: a generic LinuxCNC mill post (3-axis), separate from the Tormach PathPilot post

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
### What are you trying to do

I run a 3-axis mill on LinuxCNC 2.9 (Remora controller, `M6` remapped to an automatic tool changer) and would like to post from CamCraft straight to it. There is no plain LinuxCNC post today. The Tormach PathPilot post is the closest, but it carries Tormach assumptions, so its output has to be checked and hand-edited before it is safe on a stock LinuxCNC machine. #435 / #495 is one example: the retract assumed machine Z0 is the top of travel.

### How you imagine it working

A generic LinuxCNC mill post (e.g. `linuxcnc.cps` plus a `linuxcnc-3axis.mch` machine), written to the RS274NGC dialect as LinuxCNC documents it, with no PathPilot-specific codes. LinuxCNC machines differ a lot from one another, so the machine-specific parts would be options rather than fixed:

- **Retract and tool-change position:** `G53 G0 Z<value>` with a user value (machine Z0 is not always the top of travel), `G28`/`G30`, or none.
- **Tool change:** `T<n> M6` then `G43 H<n>`, with an option to leave out `G43` when the `M6` remap applies the tool length itself.
- **Path blending:** `G64 P<tolerance>` with a user value, or `G61` exact path.
- **Program start/end:** a safe block (`G17 G90 G40 G49 G80`, units, work offset); end with `M5 M9` and `M2` or `M30`; optional `%` delimiters.
- **Drilling and tapping:** `G81`/`G82`/`G83`/`G73`. LinuxCNC's rigid tap is `G33.1`, which needs a spindle encoder, so an option to refuse or expand taps on a machine without one.
- **Arcs:** `G2`/`G3` with incremental IJK (LinuxCNC's default `G91.1`), helices allowed.
- Comments in parentheses, no line numbers by default; spindle `M3`/`M4 S`, coolant `M7`/`M8`/`M9`.

Happy to run posted programs through a LinuxCNC 2.9 sim and air-cut them on my machine, and report back.

body:
What happens: the maintainer starts the simulation and gets this status line (2026-11-16, several times):

```
! generated 2D Adaptive1: 4269 moves (0 plunge(s), 3 level(s), 1617 arc(s)), 0 warning(s) - arc output: of 789 fitted arcs, 169 could not be proved inside the cutter-centre area, 85 would add a kink and 2 would cross another feed - those stay chords - Carried stock: the operation's top Z20.000 is below the material over its region (Z22.000) - the first descent starts over that material and feeds down; the first level engages 2.000 mm | traced playback refused: 2D Contour1: no toolpath yet - generate it first - the sheet stands
```

2D Adaptive1 has a toolpath. 2D Contour1 has none. The traced playback of the stock is refused for the whole setup, and the simulation shows no stock removal.

Three faults:

1. One operation without a toolpath stops the stock playback of each operation before it.
2. The refusal is at the end of a long line, after the notes of a different operation. The line starts with `!`, thus the notes of 2D Adaptive1 look like an error. They are notes.
3. The words "traced playback" and "the sheet stands" are not plain English for a user.

Expected:

- The stock playback runs for each operation in program order up to the first operation that has no toolpath. It does not skip an operation and continue: the stock after a skipped operation is wrong.
- A separate, short message names the operation where the playback stops and what to do: "Stock simulation stops before 2D Contour1: it has no toolpath. Generate it to see the rest."
- The generation notes of an operation do not show as an error when the operation has 0 warnings.

Safety: the stock judgment that can block the post does not change. This issue changes only what the playback shows and the message text. An operation without a toolpath does not post, as today.

Done means: a setup with a generated operation followed by an operation without a toolpath plays the stock removal of the first one, and a test pins that. A test pins the new message text. A test pins that the notes of a clean operation do not carry the error mark.

body:
What happens: in a setup whose part alignment is not "As modelled", Generate refuses some operation kinds. The maintainer reported this message on 2026-11-16, "on different operations":

```
generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: 2D Offset1: invalid machining parameters: setup 'Setup1' holds the part turned (part alignment) - 2D Offset is not supported yet in an aligned setup (Face, 2D Contour, 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive, 3D Pocket and 3D Finish are); set the setup's part alignment back to As modelled, or machine it in another setup
```

Maintainer: "why would i not be able to reorientate my part?! or rotate my WCS's.."

Expected: each operation kind generates in a setup that holds the part turned. To turn the part or the WCS is a normal step of a job.

Evidence:
- The guard is `setup_align::generation_problem` in `crates/app/src/setup_align.rs`.
- PR #2214 (#2210) removed the same guard for area controls. It found that the code already read the picks in the setup frame.
- #763 (in review) makes one machining-frame seam for part alignment and tilt. Check its PR for overlap first.

Work:
- List each operation kind that the guard refuses (2D Offset, and the others).
- For each kind, prove with a test that the generator reads its geometry in the setup frame, then remove the refusal. Use turns about more than one axis, not only 90 degrees about Z.
- If a kind does not read the setup frame, add the transform. Do not remove its refusal before that.
- The verify check and the post gate do not change.

Safety: this work changes which programs post. A kind that reads the model frame in a turned setup cuts in the wrong place. Keep the refusal for each kind that has no proof.

Done means: no operation kind refuses a setup only because the part is turned, or each kind that still refuses has its own issue. A test for each kind compares the path in a turned setup with the path of the same part modelled in that position.

title: Windowed UI slows down as operations are added, and the frame rate drops when a toolpath is selected (3 user reports; headless stays fast)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:ui

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Reported by a user on Discord (f1inch), relayed by the maintainer's collaborator on 2026-11-16; filed by an agent:

> "after i add a second operation after faceing the camcraft gets so damn slow that i cant work with it."

The user shared the project privately. It is not attached here.

## The project (shape only)

- Project version 61, 17 MB on disk.
- One model of about 45,000 triangles (8.4 MB of facets).
- One setup, one box stock, one tool (4 mm router bit).
- Two operations: `Face1`, then `2D Contour1`.
- Machine: a hobby router file (FoxAlien WM-3020), grblHAL post.

## Readings (headless, release build of main 3580f3888, Linux)

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| `open_project` | 0.1 s |
| `generate` 2D Contour1 (forced) | 1.0 s |
| `generate` Face1 (forced) | < 0.1 s |
| `verify` | 0.2 s |

So project load, generation and verification are fast. The slowness is in the windowed shell: the redraw, the scene rebuild, the toolpath or stock display, or the simulation. #164 (closed) found a similar pattern: one CPU core at 100% in the window while `camcraft-cli process` took under a second.

The project also has two problems that are not this defect:
- The model was saved before mesh fidelity was recorded (v58 or older), so the gouge check blocks the post until the model is imported again.
- `Face1` moves go outside the machine stroke (X to -47.5, Z to -4, stroke X 0..290, Z 0..70): 626 limit problems.

A large number of findings can make a UI list slow. Check if the window rebuilds or paints all 626 findings each frame.

## What is not known yet

- Which action is slow: select an operation, regenerate, rotate the view, or play the simulation.
- The user's CamCraft version, operating system and GPU (the paths suggest Linux).
- If one operation is fast and two operations are slow.

## Done means

On a fixture with the same shape (a model of about 45,000 triangles, a Face and a 2D Contour, and several hundred findings), the windowed UI stays responsive: a frame cost close to the one-operation case, no CPU core held at 100% when idle. A test pins the cost that caused it (for example the scene or findings rebuild count for each frame).

## What happens

A 3D Pocket on a blind hole whose floor is between Top Z and the first level gets no floor level. Example: depth 3 mm at stepdown 4 mm. With PR #2013 the operation is refused with "nothing to machine". Before PR #2013 the operation made one pass at Top Z in the air and did not cut the hole.

Set a stepdown that is not more than the depth of the hole.

## Safety

This work is under the safety floor. It changes the toolpath and the posted G-code of a 3D Pocket on a shallow blind hole.

## Done means

- A test shows that a blind hole of depth 3 mm at stepdown 4 mm is cut at its floor, with one level.
- `a_blind_pocket_never_enters_solid_under_any_ladder` stays green with its no-gouge assert unchanged.

title: Post engine: 1-based script errors, loop limits, blank template, and preview sample streams

labels.name: enhancement

labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Separate user post script evaluation from the prelude and add execution limits, the blank template, and built-in sample streams in `crates/post`.

## Scope

1. Update `Script::load` (`crates/post/src/post/js.rs`) to evaluate `PRELUDE`, `ROTARY_CAP`, and `EXPLAIN_JS` before evaluating user `.cps` source in a second call. Return exact 1-based user line and column numbers in script errors.
2. Apply `boa_engine::RuntimeLimits` (`set_loop_iteration_limit`, `set_recursion_limit`, `set_stack_size_limit`) before running user scripts so endless loops stop cleanly on desktop and `wasm32`. Cap maximum output lines per run.
3. Define the clean-room Blank Template constant (`description`, `vendor`, `legal`, `extension`, `capabilities = 1`, `serves = ["mill"]`, `programUnits = "mm"`, empty hooks `onOpen` through `onClose`) using public RS-274 / ISO 6983 conventions only.
4. Expose embedded preview sample `.cnc` streams built from representative committed goldens in `crates/app/tests/golden/` (dressed with setup, operation, tool, spindle, and cycle feed records like `common::legacy_program::as_program`) and a default VMC machine JSON.

## Rules

- Keep all shipped post outputs deterministic and byte-identical.
- Use only public G-code standards and existing project files (Clean-Room Protocol).

## Done means

- Tests verify exact 1-based line numbers on syntax errors and runtime exceptions in user `.cps` code.
- Tests verify that `while (true) {}` aborts cleanly with a clear error message.
- Tests verify that the Blank Template compiles and posts zero lines with zero warnings on basic milling samples.
- Tests verify that every built-in sample stream posts cleanly through `fanuc.cps` and `mazak.cps`.

Part of #2050

body:
Slice (c) of #1198. The maintainer asked for this work in his own words (quoted in #1198, 2026-11-12): "Move / Rotate should be tied to in 3D view control bar floating ontop at the bottom of the viewport."

Slice (b), PR #1330, adds the Move mode and the move handles only. No PR and no issue exists for the rotate handles.

**What is wanted**
- A Rotate mode in the bottom bar of the viewport, next to the Move button of PR #1330.
- With Rotate on and one shown part selected, the gizmo shows rotation handles (rings, or the axis balls as rotation handles). Decide, and record the decision in `docs/decisions/`.
- A drag on a handle turns the part about that axis, through the bounding-box centre of the part.

**How it must fit the laws**
- Everything Is a Command: the drag is an ephemeral preview while the button is down. The release queues ONE undoable command: the same `MoveModel` that the Model page's rotation fields run. No direct field write.
- Escape during a drag cancels with no history step. A drag that ends at its start angle adds no history step.
- The rotation changes the placement in the same way as a typed rotation: operations become stale, and stock and fixtures follow as they do now. No new placement path.
- A handle under the cursor wins the press. Empty space still orbits. The handles keep a constant size on screen.
- While the user drags, the bar shows the angle.
- If a new app command is necessary, it gets its MCP tool (AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool"). The MCP `move_model` tool already sets the rotation.
- Pin the behaviour in structural and interaction tests, not in PNG snapshots.

Depends on PR #1330 (the Move mode and the `move_drag` module). Stack on that PR, or start after it merges.

Done means: a drag on a rotation handle of the selected part turns the part about the axis, one undo step for each drag, and interaction tests pin the handles, the angle and the undo step.

Refs #1198

body:
Part of #2007.

Maintainer in chat, 2026-11-15: "That tool editor issue is a P3".

## What happens

- A tool keeps its own holder as `holder_d`/`holder_len` (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs:203-204`).
- A library holder is copied, not referenced. `SetToolBody::library` (`crates/app/src/commands/tool_body.rs:155-169`) writes the library outline into the tool as a drawn spun body. The tool keeps no link to the library entry.
- The holder fit is thus sized for each tool by hand.

## What to do

1. Add a tool key `holder: {entry, gauge_len, projection}` that names a library entry (`holder_library::find`, `crates/tools/src/holder_library.rs:345`).
2. Resolve the reference to a `HolderProfile` in the one seam: `tool_body::judged`, `stack` and `digest` (`crates/app/src/tool_body.rs:173-224`). Each collision law and the simulation (`sim_tool_body.rs:196-197`) then read the same shape.
3. Keep the #828 floor for a machine-default holder.
4. Migration: an old drawn library copy and an old `holder_d`/`holder_len` cylinder load as a custom holder with the same shape. Use the version step of the cutting-data sub-issue (`PROJECT_VERSION` 62, `.camtools` 2), or take the next one if that sub-issue is not merged.
5. A reference to an entry that does not exist refuses the file by name. It never falls back to a different holder (see #808).
6. Fill the holder fields from the entry. The user does not size them.

This changes the shape that collision checks and simulation read: `effort:max` by the safety floor.

## Done means:

- A tool with a library holder stores the reference, not a copy.
- `judged` and `stack` give the same bands for a referenced holder and for its old copy. A test pins this.
- An old project and an old `.camtools` file load with no change to any collision result. A test pins this.
- An unknown entry name refuses the file by name.
- The `set_tool_holder` MCP tool (#799) writes the reference.
- The PR is `feat!` with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

Order: after the layout sub-issue. The Weldon sub-issue needs this one.

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-15, on v0.21.0. His words:

> The tool editor page needs a re work, Input fields sitting left of the input, cutting data by material should be default behavior and the default "value" is what we have in the catalog now. We can have a material called "Unknown" that is the default value.  Why there is two previews of the tool is also strange. One drawn profile of the tool and the holder picked should be enough. The holder library, should remove the parametric holder values and "fill them in" with the values from the library.. There is no need for having a Weldon for each "sized tool".. a weldon is a weldon, and whatever tool will fit it.
> In general the Tool editor needs a complete overhaul.

This is an umbrella issue. Research it, then file one sub-issue for each part, and close this issue.

## Parts

1. **Layout.** Put each label on the left of its input field, in a property grid (see the Fusion-style dialog rule: collapsible groups, tooltips).
2. **Cutting data by material is the default.** Each tool has cutting data (speed, feed, stepdown, stepover) for each material. The current single set of values becomes the data of a material named `Unknown`. `Unknown` is the default material. Existing tool libraries and project files load with their values moved to `Unknown`, with no loss.
3. **One preview.** The editor shows one drawing: the tool profile and the holder that the user selected. Remove the second preview. (See #2005: the body and the spun profile draw over each other.)
4. **Holders come from the holder library.** The user selects a holder from the library. The holder values (diameter, length, gauge length) come from the library entry and are not typed into each tool. Remove the parametric holder fields from the tool.
5. **A holder is not sized to a tool.** One holder entry (for example a Weldon holder) serves each tool whose shank fits it. Do not keep one holder entry for each tool size. The fit check (shank diameter against the holder bore) must give a clear refusal when a tool does not fit.

## Questions for the research

- The tool library and project file format change (parts 2, 4, 5). Give the migration and the version bump. This can be a breaking change.
- How the collision check and the simulation get the holder shape after part 4. They must use the same shape that the preview shows.
- Where cutting data by material connects to the operation: the operation uses the material of the setup stock, or `Unknown` when the stock has no material.
- How this joins #2002 (tool settings in Properties, catalog in its own panel). Decide one layout for the two issues.

## Related

#2002, #2003, #2005, #93, #743, #808, #898

## Done means

Each part has a sub-issue with a priority, an effort label and a "Done means" line. This issue lists them and is closed.

body:
Add a clean-room Mach4 milling postprocessor (`assets/posts/mach4.cps`) specced solely from public Mach4 and RS-274/NGC documentation.

### Context
- `assets/posts/` and `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` contain no Mach4 or MachMotion post today.
- Standard Mach4 lacks `G43.4` RTCP, supports `G93` inverse-time feed (`F` on every feed block) and `G94`, limits `G2/G3` arcs to Cartesian planes (`G17/G18/G19`), uses `G43 H..`, `G53`/`G28`/`G30` safe retracts, and `G64` constant velocity mode.
- Depends on machine schema (#1962), AC IK solver (#1965), and `G93` timing (#1966).

### Requirements
- Author `assets/posts/mach4.cps` from public Mach4 Mill GCode Programming documentation only (Clean-Room Protocol). Register it in `BUILTINS` (`crates/app/src/posting.rs`).
- Leave 3-axis programs in standard `G94` mode with `G2/G3` arcs unchanged.
- Handle 3+2 indexed sections by retracting safely in `G94`, positioning `G0 A.. C..` (with optional unclamp/clamp M-codes), and cutting in `G94` with rotated planar coordinates and arcs.
- Handle simultaneous 5-axis sections by outputting no `G43.4`, linearizing arcs to `G1`, switching to `G93`, emitting pre-compensated `X Y Z A C` and `F` on every `G1` block, and restoring `G94` after the section.
- Respect Mach4 rotary rollover settings (`unwrapped` vs `rollover_360` option) and unwind safely only at retract `Z`.
- Refuse tilted/simultaneous posting by name if the machine lacks required trunnion geometry or states `controller.rtcp = true` unexpectedly without matching setup.

Done means: `mach4.cps` posts valid Mach4 G-code for 3-axis, 3+2 indexed, and simultaneous 5-axis sections in mm and inch, refuses missing trunnion geometry by name, and passes golden conformance tests.

body:
Implement native AI provider transport, secret handling, and transport-level offline enforcement in `crates/app`.

## Scope
- Gate native sockets, threads, and OS keychain calls under `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` so `crates/ui` continues to build on `wasm32` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_web.rs`).
- Support public cloud endpoints (`https://` only):
  - Anthropic Messages API
  - OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses APIs (GPT and Codex models)
  - Google Gemini `generateContent` API
- Support OpenAI-compatible local endpoints (`localhost` / `127.0.0.1` / `[::1]`):
  - Ollama (`http://localhost:11434/v1` plus `/api/show` capability probe)
  - Unsloth Studio (`http://127.0.0.1:8888`)
  - LM Studio (`http://localhost:1234/v1`)
  - `llama.cpp` `llama-server` (`--jinja`)
- Store API keys only in the OS keychain (`keyring` crate) or environment variables (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`). Never write secrets to `prefs.json` (`crates/app/src/prefs.rs`) or project files. Reject plain `http://` when sending keys off localhost.
- Add `ai_offline_only` to `ViewPrefs` in `crates/app/src/prefs.rs` and reject all non-loopback hosts inside the HTTP client before opening a socket.
- Use only public provider specifications and update `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` for new third-party crates.

Done means: Fake loopback HTTP server tests verify every provider wire format and Ollama capability detection, `prefs.json` stores zero keys, offline mode blocks non-loopback hosts, and `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` builds cleanly.
