title: post-merge.yml: let a running post-merge gate finish (cancel-in-progress: false), so a merge batch still gets complete results

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
**The request (mkinney, 2026-11-15):** make sure the post-merge gate runs to completion even when more merges arrive, using the one-line change below.

## What happens

`.github/workflows/post-merge.yml`:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: post-merge-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && 'main' || inputs.ref || 'main' }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

Each PR merge is its own push to main and starts its own run. With `cancel-in-progress: true`, each new merge cancels the run in progress. In a merge batch (N merges within one gate run, about 37 min), only the LAST run finishes:
- #1752: seven runs in a row were cancelled by later merges. The breaking merge had to be found by hand in a range of 6 merges, including the cut merge.
- #1909 and #1856 (2026-11-15): after the 10-PR bulk batch, the only result was for the tip. Each needed a manual search for the cause (#1839, and #1787 with #1793).

## Proposal (one line)

```yaml
  cancel-in-progress: false
```

With a concurrency group, GitHub keeps at most one run in progress and one pending:
- The run already in progress always finishes. It gives a full result for its commit.
- A newer merge waits as the single pending run. A still newer merge replaces it, so runs do not pile up.

For a batch of N merges this tests 2 points (the first merge and the last), not 1. Each run gives a result. The cost: more runner time on the self-hosted post-merge runner (no billed minutes), and the result for the batch tip arrives up to one gate-run later.

The comment at the top of the file (line 9, "tests only the newest head (cancel-in-progress)") must change with it. The cut-skip logic (`post-merge-skip.sh`) does not change.

## Later options (not part of this issue)

- A unique group per commit (no cancels at all): every merge is tested, but a 10-PR batch takes about 6 h on one runner.
- Bisect-when-red: when a run fails, test the merges between the last green run and this one, to find the breaking merge automatically.

## Done means

`cancel-in-progress: false` is on the post-merge concurrency group, the comment explains the queue behaviour, and a batch of merges shows the in-progress run finishing (not "cancelled") in the Actions history.

A `.github/` workflow change: the maintainer's decision. Agents do not edit it.

body:
Add a built-in 3-axis router post for the **RichAuto DSP A11** controller in `assets/posts/richauto.cps`. Register it in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` and pin it in `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`.

## Context

Issue #1907 confirmed that mkinney's friend runs a **RichAuto DSP A11** handheld controller. Common Laguna Swift (`4x4`, `4x8`, `5x10`) and Grizzly CNC routers (`G0894`, `G0931`, `G0895`) also use this controller.

CamCraft's existing posts (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps`, `fanuc.cps`, `carvera.cps`, `tinyg.cps`) do not run safely on a RichAuto A11:
- `grblhal.cps` emits `G91.1`, `G94`, `G53 G0 Z...`, `T<n> M6`, and canned cycles. RichAuto A11 uses the pendant `AbsCntr` menu switch (`Off` = incremental) instead of `G91.1`, and basic router firmware can reject canned cycles or `G91.1`.
- `fanuc.cps` emits `%`, `O0001`, `T.. M6`, `G43 H..`, `G49`, `G91 G28 Z0`, and `G84` tapping.

## Specification (OEM manuals only)

1. **Units and file format:** default to `mm` (`G21`) to match RichAuto's internal metric math and avoid `G20` scale errors. Write `.nc` ASCII files with parentheses comments `(...)`. Omit `%`, `O` program numbers, and `;` comments.
2. **Preamble and arcs:** write `G21`, `G90`, `G17`, `G40`, and `G80`. Omit `G91.1`, `G94`, `G43`, and `G49`. Emit incremental `I`/`J`/`K` matching `AbsCntr = Off`. Handle `G54` cleanly (`G54` default or document `Read G54` vs `Ign G54` in post notes; handle or refuse multi-WCS safely).
3. **Spindle and warm-up:** write `S<rpm> M3`. Add a configurable spindle dwell property (`G04 P<ms>`, default `0`) so the post works alongside the pendant `Spindle Delay` setting. Document 8-step `S1`-`S8` VFD wiring in post comments.
4. **Drilling and tool changes:** expand all canned drill cycles (`G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G73`, `G86`, `G89`) to plain `G0`/`G1` moves (using the pattern in `assets/posts/carvera.cps` and `tinyg.cps`). Refuse mid-program tool changes on the initial 3-axis manual slice (or lift Z cleanly and write `M0` with `(CHANGE TOOL T<n>)` rather than bare `T<n> M6`).
5. **Refusals and footer:** refuse `G84` tapping, `G41`/`G42` cutter compensation, and probing. Retract Z to clearance height in work coordinates, stop spindle (`M5`) and coolant (`M9` if active), and end with `M30` (no trailing `%`).

## Rules

- Clean room: use only RichAuto DSP A11 OEM documentation, RS-274 / ISO 6983 standards, and CamCraft repository patterns (`assets/posts/AGENTS.md`). Do not read or copy Autodesk, HSMWorks, or third-party CAM posts.

## Done means

- `assets/posts/richauto.cps` exists and registers in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs`.
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` passes for `RichAuto DSP A11` across all mill goldens and refuses `G84`, `G41`/`G42`, and probing by name.
- Posted `.nc` output uses `G21`, incremental `I`/`J`, expanded drilling moves, `(...)` comments, safe Z retract, and `M30` with no `%`, `O` headers, `G91.1`, `G43`, or `G49`.
- Decision entry added under `docs/decisions/`.

Part of #1907

body:
**The request (mkinney, 2026-11-15):** "My friend has a table like that. It's similar to Laguna Swift or Grizzly. Can you open a research only issue to research Laguna and Grizzly CNC machines? I can probably have him do test cuts."

**Research, not code.** Pick never takes this issue. It is answered in comments, then broken into sub-issues (AGENTS.md "needs-research"). A real machine is available through mkinney for test cuts. The exact model and controller of the friend's machine are still to be confirmed (open question 1).

## Why

CamCraft has machine files and posts for hobby routers (Sienci AltMill/grblHAL, Makera Carvera, TinyG, Tormach 24R) but none for the Laguna or Grizzly CNC router lines. These are common full-size shop routers (4x4 and 4x8 tables). Their controllers and G-code differ from LinuxCNC/PathPilot.

## Open questions

1. **The friend's machine:** make, model, table size, spindle (power, rpm range, collet), the tool changer (manual, or ATC on some Swift models), and the CONTROLLER. Ask for a photo of the controller or pendant and of its "about" or version screen.
2. **Controllers in these lines** (from public documentation only): which controllers each Laguna Swift and Grizzly CNC model ships with (for example a handheld DSP controller, Mach3/Mach4, UCCNC, or a maker-specific controller). For each one: the G-code dialect, supported G/M codes, arcs (I/J, R, the plane), canned cycles, work offsets, tool length offsets, units, the line-number and comment rules, and the file size and transfer limits (USB, line length).
3. **Machine data for a machine file:** X/Y/Z travel, max feeds and rapids, spindle range, the tool change position, and the origin conventions (the corner, Z0 at the table or the stock top).
4. **Post needs:** what our generic posts already produce that would run, and what must differ (the preamble, the spindle start and warm-up, M6 and tool change handling, the end of program, safe Z).
5. **Work flow:** how the operator sets the work zero, touches off tools (a Z puck or a fixed sensor), and loads files.
6. **Test-cut plan:** a short, safe set of test programs for the friend's machine, made with CamCraft: an air cut first, then foam or MDF. What to measure and report (the controller accepts the file, arcs are correct, the scale is correct, the tool change behaves).

## Clean-room rules

- **Used:** Laguna's and Grizzly's public documentation (manuals, spec sheets, published support articles), the controller makers' public manuals, general CNC knowledge, and the friend's own test results.
- **Not used:** any Autodesk Fusion or HSMWorks post or output, and third-party CAM post processors (Fusion, Vectric VCarve/Aspire, others) for these machines. Do not copy text from manuals. Cite and summarise only.

## Sub-issues to file (when the research is done)

- Machine file(s) for the friend's model (and the common sizes of the line).
- A post for the controller, or a variant of an existing post, with goldens.
- A test-cut kit for the friend (the programs plus a one-page check sheet). The results come back via mkinney.
- A docs section: the router first part (with the AltMill/grblHAL page).

**Done means:** every open question has an answered comment, the friend's controller is confirmed, the sub-issues are filed with "Part of #this", and this umbrella is closed.

body:
**The request (mkinney, 2026-11-15):** "Can we have better docs on how to do 3+1 and continuous 4 axis milling? ... I want to use my microArc4." The user has a Tormach 770MX with a microARC 4 (machine file `assets/machines/tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch`).

Today the pages are short: `multi-axis/indexed.md` (101 lines), `continuous-4-axis.md` (74 lines) and `machines-and-tcp.md` (83 lines). They name the microARC 4 only once or twice. There is no complete worked example.

Wanted: two step-by-step walkthroughs on the 770MX + microARC 4, each with a small committed demo project and images (see the example-images issue):
1. **Indexed 3+1:** a part with features on several faces (for example a hex or a square bar with holes and pockets on four sides).
   - Mount the part between centres or in a chuck on the A axis. Set the work offset on the rotary centreline (how to find it and probe it).
   - Make one setup per index angle, or one setup with indexed operations. The guide says which one CamCraft prefers and why.
   - How the post writes the A moves (unwind, clamp/unclamp if any, safe retract before an index).
   - The checks: collision with the rotary and tailstock, and reach.
2. **Continuous 4-axis:** wrapping (an engraving or a slot wrapped on a cylinder) and a rotary roughing or finishing pass.
   - The operation choices, the feed-rate mode (inverse time or degrees per minute, and what the 770MX post writes), and the A-axis feed cap.
   - Simulation and verify for 4-axis, and what a refusal means here.
3. **Machine setup:** the microARC 4 machine file fields (A axis direction, limits, max rpm and feed), and the PathPilot settings to check before the first run.
4. **Prove it out:** a dry run in the PathPilot Hub 770MX simulator with the 4th axis enabled. Which numbers to check: the A-axis direction and the wrap scale.

Clean room: CamCraft behaviour, Tormach's public documentation and general machining knowledge only.

Done means: both walkthroughs are on the site with demo projects and images. Each posted program runs to M30 in the PathPilot Hub 770MX simulator with the microARC 4 (record the run on the issue). The pages link from the guide's Multi-axis section.

body:
Maintainer request from #1452 ("We should be able to load DXF file to do profile cuts on.").

Depends on #1860 and #1861.

## Goal
Store DXF drawings as `Sketch` entities in `camcraft-app`, persist them in `.camproj`, add the undoable `ImportDxf` command, and expose `import_dxf` on MCP and scripting.

## Scope
- Add a `Sketch` component to `crates/app/src/schema.rs` and register it in `register_schema`. Keep `Sketch` separate from `Facets` so 3D solid tools never treat a 2D drawing as a zero-triangle mesh.
- Store normalized 2D primitives, layer names, chaining tolerance, chained loops/runs from #1861, source DXF units, and import summary counts on `Sketch`. Place the entity on the XY plane with `Location` (`pos`, `rot`) and setup alignment support (`crates/app/src/setup_align.rs`).
- Add `EntityKind::Sketch` to `crates/app/src/project/file.rs` and an optional `sketch` field on `EntityDto` (`crates/app/src/project/entity.rs`). Bump `PROJECT_VERSION` cleanly in `crates/app/src/project/apply.rs` so existing project files load unchanged.
- Implement `ImportDxf::new(path, unit_override)` in `crates/app/src/commands/` following `ImportModel` (`crates/app/src/commands/import_model.rs`). Validate input before mutating `History`. Return a typed missing-units error when `$INSUNITS` is absent or unitless (`0`) and the caller omits `unit_override`.

title: Tormach lathe G76 refusal for a thread record cached before #517 does not tell the user to regenerate the operation

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
## What happens

PR #517 changes the meaning of the thread record field `finish_allowance`. It is now the finishing pass's own depth, and it is never 0 on a new record. The Tormach lathe post (`assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps`) accepts a G76 record only when `finish_allowance` is the last step of its own ladder.

An operation that was generated before PR #517 has `finish_allowance` 0 in its cached record. The stale stamp (`crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs`, `current_stamp`) hashes only the inputs and has no generator version. Thus the operation reads Fresh, and the Tormach post refuses it by name. The refusal is safe, but its message does not tell the user to regenerate the operation. The user cannot see the fix from the message.

Found in the full review of PR #517 (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/517#pullrequestreview-5910390160), note "Old projects".

## Expected

The refusal tells the user what to do: regenerate the threading operation. Alternative: the stamp carries a generator version, so that such an operation reads Stale.

## Done means

- A Tormach G76 refusal for a record with `finish_allowance` 0 (a record cached before PR #517) tells the user to regenerate the operation.
- A test posts such a record and asserts the text of the refusal.
- The Fanuc post's behaviour for the same record (it writes `R0`, the output of main before PR #517) does not change in this issue.

title: Tormach lathe G76 (inch): floored J makes LinuxCNC cut ceil(K/J) = 4 passes where the record verified 3

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
What happens: `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps` (`g76Grid`) takes J (first depth) to the grid with `floor` and K from the rounded peak and outward-rounded root, each on its own. LinuxCNC's `R1` (constant depth) ladder cuts J, 2J, ... clamped at K, so it cuts ceil(K/J) passes. The inch golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/thread_g76_inch.nc` posts `G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0314 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0`: 0.0944 / 0.0314 = 3.006, so the control cuts 0.0314, 0.0628, 0.0942 and a 0.0944 pass (0.0002 in on diameter), 4 passes where the record laid and the verdict judged 3 (0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2 mm radius). The mm golden (`J0.8 K2.4`) is exact.

Not a gouge: the extra pass is shallower than the root and the root is rounded outward. But the posted words state a pass schedule that was not verified, the same class of mismatch #417 removes on the Fanuc lathe (PR #517 review, where the Fanuc inch R was fixed by deriving it from the rounded words' own ladder).

Expected: the grid words' own ladder cuts exactly the record's pass count: e.g. choose J (and K within the outward-root rule) so ceil(K/J) equals the record's rung count, or refuse by name when the grid cannot state it. Semantics from the LinuxCNC G76 documentation (R1 = constant depth, K = full depth).

Note: the inch golden was run on the PathPilot Hub 8L sim to M30 with no alarm (PR #517 comments); that run does not check the pass count. A fix changes that golden and needs a new Hub run.

Found while fixing the M3 review of PR #517 (#417); left out of that PR because its Tormach goldens must stay byte-identical to main.

Done means: the Tormach inch G76 words make LinuxCNC's ladder cut exactly the record's passes (a test parses the posted J/K and counts ceil(K/J) against the record), or the record is refused by name; mm output unchanged.

title: post-merge.yml: the report job is skipped when the gate fails, so a red main opens no issue

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
What happens: post-merge run 43535610115 (push to main at 745edc36a) ended with job `gate` = failure and job `report` = skipped. The rolling issue `main is red (post-merge gate)` was not opened or commented on.

Expected: AGENTS.md "Fixes are tested in the background": a red post-merge gate opens or comments on the rolling issue; the next green run closes it.

Cause (read from `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml` on main): the `report` job has `needs: gate` and an `if:` with no status-check function:

```
if: ${{ (needs.gate.result == 'success' || needs.gate.result == 'failure') && needs.gate.outputs.skipped != 'true' && (...) }}
```

GitHub Actions adds an implicit `success()` to a job's `if` unless it contains `always()`, `failure()`, `cancelled()` or `!cancelled()`. With a failed `needs` job the implicit `success()` is false, so the job is skipped before the expression is read. The job therefore only ever runs on green.

Suggested fix: start the condition with `always() &&` (the rest already excludes cancelled and skipped runs). One line.

Note on this particular run: its only red test was `a_lowered_cap_refuses_the_same_face_at_once` (`crates/app/tests/import_step_guard.rs`, "not within 30s"), the wall-clock flake of issue 1605, so main was not truly red here. The reporting gap is real for any failure.

A `.github/` change: the PR is read, not built, and waits for the maintainer (`needs-maintainer`). `Process change: yes` does not apply (`.github/` is not a process file).

Found by the maintenance session while watching runs.

Done means: a post-merge run whose gate fails runs `report` and opens or comments on the rolling issue; a green run after it closes that issue; a cancelled or cut-skipped run still reports nothing.

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "we should be able to set start points on generated path and also exit points.. So the path gets regenerated to those."

What is missing: where an operation starts cutting and where it leaves is chosen by the generator alone. The user cannot say "enter here" or "leave here", for example to keep the entry mark off a visible face, to start a contour away from a clamp, or to end next to the following feature.

Wanted: on the operations where it has a meaning (2D Contour, Pocket, Adaptive, Face, Slot, Bore, and the 3D finishing passes that have a free start), two optional picks:
- Start point(s): picked in the viewport (a point on the model, a sketch point or typed coordinates). For a closed contour the path is re-sequenced to begin at the pick's nearest point on the chain, with its lead-in there; for a pocket or adaptive region the entry (helix, ramp or plunge) is placed at the pick. One pick per chain or region; chains with no pick keep the automatic choice.
- Exit point(s): the same for where the pass ends and the lead-out is placed.

Changing a pick is an undoable command (it edits the operation parameters) and regenerates the path. MCP: the same parameters on the operation tools.

Safety: a pick is a wish, never an override of a check. If the entry, lead or ramp at the picked place does not fit (helix does not fit in the region, lead-in gouges a wall, the point is outside the machinable region or inside a keep-out or fixture), the operation is refused by name or marked incomplete, saying which pick and why; it never moves the entry silently and never posts a path that the collision or gouge checks would refuse at the automatic entry.

Related: the companion issue on pre-drilled holes as entry positions (filed with this one).

Done means: a closed 2D contour with a picked start begins and leads in at that point and, with a picked exit, leads out there (golden CL); a pocket enters at its picked point; an impossible pick is refused by name in a test; undo and redo restore the previous path; the MCP tools take the picks; the structural UI test covers the two pick rows.

body:
Asked for by the maintainer in chat (2026-11-12), filed by an agent for him, at the priority he gave: "issue; enhancement; P4; Ability to move a body by dragging around the window using the gizmos each end of the "axis" should have a small round ball to "grab onto" so we can drag the model in that direction.. Move / Rotate should be tied to in 3D view control bar floating ontop at the bottom of the viewport. We should also move the buttons to the right in the view port to a ribbon "overlay" at the bottom instead in the shape of a gray background rounded corners with buttons ontop of it."

**What is wanted**
1. **Drag to move.** A selected body shows a gizmo; each end of each axis has a small round ball to grab. Dragging a ball moves the body along that axis.
2. **Move / Rotate modes** chosen from a control bar that floats over the bottom of the 3D viewport. Rotate uses the same gizmo (rings or the balls as rotation handles - decide and record).
3. **A bottom overlay bar.** The buttons that today sit at the right edge of the viewport (frame, shaded/wireframe and the others there) move into that same overlay: a grey background with rounded corners and the buttons on top of it, at the bottom of the viewport.

**How it must fit the laws**
- Everything Is a Command: a drag is a PREVIEW while the mouse is down (ephemeral, immediate-mode) and ONE undoable command on release - the same model-transform command the Model page's position/rotation fields queue, never a field poke. Escape during a drag cancels with no history step; a zero-length drag adds none.
- Moving a body changes where the part sits: operations generated before the move must read as stale (as they do when the fields are edited); anything derived from the model's placement (the stock "from model", the raw-stock-only mark of #1094 that is void after a move, fixtures located on the part) behaves exactly as with a typed-in move. No new placement path.
- What may be dragged: models, and (decide, with the reason) fixtures and the stock. The work origin already has its own page; do not move it with this gizmo unless the maintainer says so.
- Picking a ball must not fight orbit/pan: a ball under the cursor wins, empty space still orbits. Handles keep a constant size on screen. Snapping (to a grid step, to 90 degrees for rotate) with a modifier key is a parameter with a default, shown in the bar.
- The number is still there: while dragging, the bar shows the distance or angle, and typing a value applies it exactly (same command).
- Layering ui -> app; MCP already moves a model through the transform command - if a new command is added it gets its MCP tool.
- Pixel goldens of the viewport differ at the next cut; pin the behaviour in structural / interaction tests (handles present for a selected body, a drag queues exactly one transform command with the dragged distance, Escape queues none, the overlay holds the buttons that used to be on the right).

body:
PR #913 (`Refs #900`) makes `cargo xtask gate` use sccache as a shared compile cache when it is on PATH, and lightens the dev profile (line-table debug info for our crates, none for dependencies, dependency `opt-level` 1). It was written and measured on Windows only; the maintainers have no Linux machine. This issue is for a contributor on Linux.

What to do, on the PR's branch (`issue/900-build-cache`) or on `main` once #913 is merged:
1. Without sccache installed: `cargo xtask gate quick --dry-run` and one real `cargo xtask gate test <any test name>` - the gate must run exactly as before (no wrapper set, no error).
2. Install sccache, then build the same test binary from an empty `target/` twice in two different checkouts or worktrees: note the cold time, the second (warm cache) time, the `sccache --show-stats` hit rate and the `target/` size. Do not export `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` as an environment variable (sccache hashes `CARGO_*` variables; on Windows that gave 0 cross-worktree hits).
3. Check the opt-outs: `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1` and a pre-set `RUSTC_WRAPPER` must both win.
4. Check a panic backtrace of a failing test still shows file:line with the new debug settings.
5. Is the C code (flecs, built through `cc`) cached on Linux? On Windows/MSVC it is not.

Report the numbers and anything that broke as a comment here (and on #913 if it is still open). A fix, if one is needed, is a small PR against `xtask/` (a process file: bump `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`).

Windows numbers for comparison are in PR #913's body.

Done means: the five points above are answered for Linux in a comment, and any breakage has a PR or its own issue.

title: One machining-frame seam: OpFrame composes part_alignment and TiltedFrame

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
# One machining-frame seam: OpFrame composes part_alignment and TiltedFrame

## What

The part-alignment machinery (#326) and the per-operation tilt frame (the
3+2 index, M5.1 B) both exist and both work — but only separately.
`setup_align::generation_problem` allows generation in an aligned setup for
exactly four kinds (Face, 2D Contour, 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive), and tilt
inside an aligned setup is refused outright. Every other planar kind,
picks, and area controls are refused by name. The refusals are a
verification gap, not a mathematical one: the two mechanisms compose as
plain function composition.

This issue builds ONE seam — `OpFrame`, `crates/app/src/operation/frame.rs`
— that composes the two existing mechanisms and becomes the single door
the generators' world reads go through. No generator rewrites: the motion
generators take data (facets, regions, heights); only the app read/wrap
seam moves.

## The frame contract

Coordinate systems:

- **D** — document frame (as modelled). Part entities carry their
  `Location` in D.
- **S** — setup frame: the table frame, also the world the CL stream and
  the post speak. Stock, WCS and fixtures are setup FURNITURE — stored in
  S already (#326's law; their world reads are correct and stay untouched).
- **L** — local machining frame: XY = the cutting plane, +Z = the tool
  axis. Exists only when the op tilts.

Point maps (right-to-left application, the `setup_align::compose`
convention):

- D → S: `A` = the setup's `part_alignment`, baked into part geometry
  reads (`facets_in` and siblings). Never inverted — the CL never maps
  back to D.
- S → L: `T` = `TiltedFrame` from `op.params.tilt()` (`to_local`), applied
  AFTER the alignment read: `p_L = T(A(p_D))`.
- L → S (CL out): `T.to_world`, the tilt's inverse. The whole CL stream
  wraps through `TiltedFrame::world_path`; identity when no tilt exists.

Layers stay separate (never a fourth):

1. part_alignment — setup, physical (how the part is clamped)
2. WCS — program zero (translation today)
3. operation tool orientation — the `Tilt` param

Machine-side relations remain derived internal transforms composed from
these; no user-facing SCS, no second offset frame.

## Design conditions (from the plan review)

1. **Heights and bounding boxes resolve against fully transformed
   geometry** (local bounds of `T(A(f))`), never a bare `z − origin.z`
   shift — a Z shift is not generally correct for an arbitrarily tilted
   plane. `OpFrame`'s height and AABB reads implement this from day one.
2. **Machine capability gates are preserved and pinned by tests**: a
   tilted orientation never silently posts as plain XYZ when the machine
   cannot reach it. The post's tilted-record refusals (non-RTCP, no
   rotary) keep their verdicts.
3. **Stepwise integration**: Phase 1 wires the seam behind the four
   currently-supported kinds, byte-identical. Refusals lift only as their
   numeric tests land: picks in aligned setups next, then further 2D/3D
   families, alignment × tilt last.

## Phases

- **Phase 1 (first branch)**: `OpFrame` + the four kinds through it,
  behavior byte-identical; the seam's math pinned by unit tests (identity,
  90°/180° alignment, alignment × tilt composition, transformed picks,
  local heights on tilted planes, AABBs under arbitrary rotation, CL
  back-transform, tool direction, capability gates, byte-identity).
- **Phase 2**: the selection walk reads picked parts through the seam
  (`facets_in`); picks in aligned setups verified. Tilt × picks stays
  refused.
- **Phase 3**: `verified_kind` extended kind by kind (whole-model 3D
  kinds first), each with a pinned numeric test; area controls; then tilt
  × alignment.
- **Phase 4**: re-evaluate #760 (rotated-offset carry) on top of the
  unified seam — normal 3-axis work needs alignment coverage, not offset
  rotation.

## Done means (Phase 1)

- `crates/app/src/operation/frame.rs` exists with the contract above;
  `collect_job` reads geometry/heights for the four kinds through it.
- The mandatory test list above is green.
- Existing aligned-setup tests (#326's) and goldens pass unchanged —
  byte-identical output.
- No refusal lifted, no post change, no generator change.

Related: #326 (part alignment), #316 (setup-to-setup transform), #315
(rotation refusal at the post), #760 (rotated-offset carry — re-evaluated
in phase 4, untouched by this issue's branches).

title: Tool and holder bodies as a spun profile: show them revolved in simulation, and turn an imported STEP body into an editable half-profile (DXF with a centreline)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: area:ui

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Requested by the maintainer.

## 1. Simulation shows the tool and holder as spun profiles
While simulating, draw the **tool and its holder as revolved bodies**: the half-profile spun about the spindle axis, at the tool's position and orientation each frame. Today's simulation doesn't show them as solids. Use the same profile the collision laws judge (the revolved envelope, #368), so what you see is what is checked.

## 2. Imported tool bodies and holders become an editable half-profile
When a tool body or holder is imported as **STEP**, convert it to a **2D half-profile on a centreline** (the meridian of the revolved envelope: radius against height along the tool axis). Store it as a **DXF**, with the centreline as its own entity/layer, so the profile can be edited (in the spun-profile editor, #93) and re-exported.

- Only the half-profile is editable, and the body is always its revolution about the centreline.
- Conversion should be conservative: the profile is the outer envelope (max radius at each height), never smaller than the solid, so collision checks stay safe. Non-revolved features (flats, coolant holes, the holder's drive slots) are enveloped, never cut away. Say so in the UI.
- Refuse by name when the STEP body has no clear axis (axis detection/alignment: #370) instead of guessing one.
- A tool/holder can also be **imported directly as a DXF half-profile** (a centreline plus an open profile on one side of it).
- DXF read/write is our own, written from the published DXF reference (entities `LINE`, `ARC`, `LWPOLYLINE`, layers). The minimum needed is lines and arcs, with a named refusal for anything else (splines, unclosed profiles that cross the centreline).

## Related
- #93 spun (revolved-profile) design editor for tool and holder shapes: the editor for these profiles.
- #361 import vendor STEP tool models; #368 a vendor holder judged by its revolved envelope (closed); #370 align a vendor STEP by its tool coordinate systems; #371 pick tip and axis on an imported body (closed).
- Fixtures get the same treatment in a sibling issue.

## Done means
- The simulation draws the tool and holder as revolved solids from their profiles (structural/paint assertion where possible, hand-tested by the maintainer; no snapshot PNG changes).
- Importing a STEP holder produces a DXF half-profile with a centreline, and the envelope encloses the original solid (a test samples the STEP mesh and checks every point lies inside the revolved profile).
- A DXF half-profile imports as a tool/holder body; malformed DXF (no centreline, spline, crossing profile) is a named error in a test, never a panic.
- Round trip: STEP → DXF → body → DXF is stable within tolerance.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.

title: Launch terminal is silent while the app works - add real debug logging (tracing) to stdout

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
## What happens
When CamCraft is started from a terminal, the terminal tells you almost nothing
about what the app is doing. There is no logging framework in the workspace at
all: no `log` or `tracing` dependency in any Cargo.toml, no subscriber
init in the binaries - just ~185 ad-hoc `println!`/`eprintln!` calls scattered
across crates (cli.rs, gpu_init.rs, shell.rs, the post bin). If a subsystem
decides, refuses, retries, or fails to write a file, no line reaches the
console and the failure is only discovered later by forensics on the output.

## Why now (session of 2026-11-07)
Two incidents this week were diagnosed only by reading source afterwards,
because the console was silent during them:
- **A file did not get saved when post processing** - the post appeared to
  succeed; nothing in the terminal said which path it wrote (or that it wrote
  nothing at all).
- **A limit was hit while generating operations** - the generator aborted on a
  budget/limit; the terminal showed no trace of which cap fired or what the
  result was downgraded to.

Prime Directive says "log diagnostics, never silence" - today we cannot.

## Expected
The launching terminal streams debug-level logs of app activity, filterable:
- project save / post write: source path, destination, bytes, or the reason
  nothing was written;
- operation generation: start, end, duration, which limits/budgets stopped a
  generator and what fallback took over;
- verify/sim refusals: the rule that fired and the numbers behind it;
- commands executing (name + affected entities) at debug level.

## Suggested shape
`tracing` + `tracing_subscriber` fmt layer writing to stderr at startup of the
UI binary, default level `info`, overridable by `RUST_LOG` (or a camcraft
config/env of our own). Instrument the command dispatch seam, generators, and
post entry points - the crates are already split (M4.1), so each takes its own
span targets (`camcraft_app::post`, `camcraft_motion::adaptive`, ...). Keep
hot generation loops behind level gates - logging must not slow generation.

## Done means
- Launching the app and running a post writes terminal lines naming the file
  path and result; a failed/skipped write says why.
- Hitting a generation budget (e.g. an Adaptive limit) prints which limit and
  what happened next.
- Levels are controlled by env var, default output stays quiet at `info`, and
  the batch gate shows no measurable generation slowdown.

Found while debugging the post-save incident (user request, 2026-11-07).
